entries.abstract: Two explicit simple graphs on 378 vertices have equal ordinary U-polynomials and different loopy polynomials, refuting Conjecture 8.1 of Kirillov, Nenashev, Shapiro and Vaintrob (arXiv:2609.07728v2). Lean proves equality of their full finite-palette Tutte coloring sums and inequality of their two-color loopy evaluations modulo seven. The project also proves the specialization's loopy deletion–contraction rule.
entries.title: A counterexample to the loopy and U-polynomial equivalence conjecture

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof that for the random Littlewood polynomial f_n(z) = sum_{k <= n} eps_k z^k with independent uniform signs eps_k, it is not true that almost surely R_n / log n -> 2/pi, where R_n is the number of distinct real roots of f_n (the formal-conjectures statement Erdos521.erdos_521), and the same with R_n counted with multiplicity. For odd n = 2K - 1 the proof conditions on a cone event for the top coefficients (a two-dimensional walk staying in a quadrant, probability of order 1/K), bounds the real roots on that event by Descartes' rule of signs applied to f times a square of 1 + X + ... + X^N, estimates the sign-change probabilities of the resulting coefficient sums by Fourier inversion, and concludes with a second-moment (Kochen-Stone) argument that R_n < 0.63 log n + 2 infinitely often with positive probability.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 521 is false (random ±1 polynomials, R_n / log n does not converge to 2/π almost surely)

entries.abstract: Lean formalizations of eight structural results of Chen and Shan on graph completion and decomposition. They cover robust realization of degree sequences, regular auxiliary completion, tripartite absorption and fractional and approximate triangle decomposition, bounded signed edge weights in dense bipartite graphs, and retention of prescribed edges in a perfect matching.
entries.title: Auxiliary completion, triangle absorption, and matching retention

entries.abstract: For every sufficiently large uniformity r, the closure of the ordinary Turán densities obtained by forbidding one finite r-uniform hypergraph equals the set obtained by forbidding arbitrary families. Both sets consist of zero and the closed interval from r!/r^r to one. Every family density can therefore be approximated to any positive accuracy by forbidding a single hypergraph. The threshold in r is uniform over all families and accuracies.
entries.title: The closure of the single-forbidden Turán spectrum in large uniformities

entries.abstract: Complete Lean 4 formalization disproving the Fanelli-Moscardelli tight threshold conjecture (google-deepmind/formal-conjectures Issue #7848) and determining the exact full-parity rank-improvement stability threshold K(N) = ceil(N/2) - 1 for all N >= 13 (both even N = 2m >= 14 and odd N = 2m - 1 >= 13), together with K(2m) <= m - 1 for all m >= 7.
entries.title: Disproof and Exact Threshold for the Fanelli-Moscardelli Approximate Stable Roommates Conjecture

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of an exact decision procedure, on an explicit word RAM, for the connectivity of the perfect matchings of a hexagonal plane graph under hexagonal face flips. A hexagonal plane graph is a finite simple graph with a rotation system satisfying Euler's formula |V| + |F| = |E| + 2 (F the set of faces), a designated outer face and a designated set of other faces (the defects), such that every remaining face is a hexagon, bounded by six darts with six distinct tails; the graph is 2-connected, every vertex has degree 2 or 3, and a vertex of degree 2 lies on the outer face or on a defect. A hexagonal face flip replaces a perfect matching M, in which a hexagonal face alternates, by M with the matched and unmatched edges of that face exchanged; the graph is flip connected if every perfect matching is reached from every other by hexagonal face flips. One theorem is compared: there are six fixed word programs for a word RAM (unit cost per instruction, natural registers and memory cells bounded by a word bound W along the run; the machine also has exact real registers, and a word program contains no instruction that uses them) such that (i) isPrime, on the input [q], prints [1] if q is prime and [0] otherwise, within 8 floor(sqrt q) + 16 steps whenever W >= 4q + 8; (ii) for every hexagonal plane graph with n vertices and edge set E and every numbering of its faces, darts and vertices, orient (on a fixed encoding of the rotation system), ray (on that encoding and the number of a defect) and, for every prime p, defect and z = 1 or z = -1, the chain signs, build, detMod (each reading what the previous program printed) run within the stated step and word bounds (225n + 99 and 189n + 86 steps for orient and ray; 84n + 18, 9n^2 + 66n + 21 and 11n^3 + 37n^2 + 12n floor(log2 p) + 62n + 17 steps for the chain), the chain printing one word; (iii) the first 2|E| + 3 primes are at most 16 (2|E| + 3)^2; and (iv) the graph is flip connected exactly when, for each of the first 2|E| + 3 primes, the words printed for z = 1 and z = -1 agree for every defect. The programs compute the determinants, modulo p, of the signed adjacency matrices of a Kasteleyn orientation with the edges crossed by the ray weighted by z; the theorem itself states only the runs and the exact decision. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Flip connectivity of perfect matchings under hexagonal face flips, decided exactly by Pfaffians modulo the first 2|E| + 3 primes, on a word RAM, in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof that for independent X ~ Bin(k, 1-p) and Y ~ Bin(k, p), k >= 1, 0 < g < 1 and 0 < l <= (1+g)/2, f_k(p) = P((1+g)X + lY > k) is strictly decreasing in p on [0, 1], which answers MathOverflow question 478827 (g, l in (0,1), g >= l) positively, both for the explicit binomial sum and for Mathlib's binomial measure; and that strict (even weak) decrease fails for k = 10, g = 1/7, l = 99/100, so the general claim (Fact 1 of Arigapudi, Heller and Schreiber, arXiv:2107.08423) does not hold for all g, l in (0,1).

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof that for P = N(-mu, 1) and Q = N(mu, 1) truncated to an interval [a, b] (a < b), or to any interval of positive length, d_H^2(P,Q) <= d_H(P,Q) <= d_TV(P,Q) with d_TV = (1/2)||P - Q||_1 and d_H^2 = (1/2)||sqrt P - sqrt Q||_2^2, strictly d_H < d_TV for mu != 0, which answers MathOverflow question 184460 positively; and the inequality behind it: for a log-concave f >= 0 on R with f cosh integrable and integral of f sinh zero, (int f cosh)(int f cosh - int f) <= (int f |sinh|)^2, strictly for strictly log-concave f.

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof that for finitely supported couplings (X, Y) with E[Y | X] = X and mu(Y) = E[X | Y], a convex (or continuous) f : R -> R satisfies E[f(X) - f(mu(Y))] <= E[f(Y) - f(X)] for every coupling iff f is a quadratic a t^2 + b t + c with a >= 0 (Theorem 1); the same characterisation holds for the smaller class Y = X + Z with Z independent of X and E Z = 0 (Theorem 2); and x^4, which is convex with convex second derivative, is a counterexample to the conjecture of the asker of MathOverflow question 451543.

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof that for coprime m, d with d odd, and integers r1, r2 of multiplicative order exactly d modulo m with gcd(r_i - 1, m) = 1, if prod_{u=1}^{d-1} (xi^k - xi^{k r1^u})(xi^k - xi^{-k r1^u}) = prod_{u=1}^{d-1} (xi^k - xi^{k r2^u})(xi^k - xi^{-k r2^u}) for all integers k, where xi = exp(2 pi i/m), then r1^c = r2 mod m for some c, that is, r1 and r2 generate the same subgroup of (Z/m)^x. This proves the conjecture of MathOverflow question 503314 for every odd d and every m; the cases d an odd prime (Ikeda 1980) and (Z/m)^x cyclic (Colantonio and Lauret) were known. The identity comes from the spectra of lens spaces.
entries.title: The odd-d conjecture of MathOverflow 503314 on products over powers of a root of unity

entries.abstract: For e, n >= 1 let S_e(n) be the mean of the least residues of the e-th powers modulo n, s_e(n) = #{k < n : n | k^e} and defect_e(n) = (n - s_e(n))/2 - S_e(n). The development proves, for every e and every n >= 1, the divisor form defect_e(n) = sum_{d | n} G_e(d), where G_e(d) is a sawtooth sum of the Moebius-inverted counts of e-th roots modulo d. For odd e it gives G_e = 0, so that S_e(n) = (n - s_e(n))/2. For every e >= 1 and n >= 1 it gives the closed form G_e(n) = - sum_tau [psi_tau odd] B_1(psi_tau) prod_{p | n} W_p(tau), a sum over choices of local Dirichlet characters chi_p modulo prime powers p^c dividing n, with explicit local weights built from psi_tau(p). Only the odd primitive characters with psi^e = 1 contribute. The proof is elementary: - root counts modulo prime powers (dilation, vanishing, small levels); - character orthogonality for the unit counts; - changeLevel for the primitive part; - the inflation, dilation and parity properties of the sawtooth functional. For e = 2 the result is the formula of the MeanResidue release, which is Proposition A.2 (a = 1) of Skoruppa and Zagier. For prime moduli the evaluation is classical. No statement for e >= 3 and composite n was found in the literature. Nothing is quoted.
entries.title: MeanPowerResidue: the mean e-th power residue modulo any n

entries.abstract: A connected graph G on n vertices is 3-good if its Ramsey number against the triangle, R(K_3, G), equals 2n - 1, the smallest possible value. Following Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp, let f(n) be the largest number of edges of a connected 3-good graph on n vertices, and let F(n) be the largest q such that every connected graph on n vertices with at most q edges is 3-good. Erdős Problem 1182 asks to estimate f(n) and F(n) and whether F(n)/n tends to infinity. This formalization proves, for the statements of the problem in Formal Conjectures, that f(n) = Θ(n^{3/2} (log n)^{1/2}), that F(n) = Θ(n), and that F(n)/n does not tend to infinity, together with five supporting statements (the trivial bound R(K_3, G) ≥ 2n - 1, Chvátal's theorem for trees and K_3, F(n) ≥ n - 1, and the two bounds for f(n) of Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp). The lower bound for f(n) and all results about F(n) are known. The upper bound f(n) = O(n^{3/2} (log n)^{1/2}) was not in the refereed literature when the proof was written; the best published bound was O(n^{3/2} log n), from a theorem of Sudakov. It is proved by following the triangle-free process on K_N for about N^{3/2} (log N)^{1/2} steps, with all concentration estimates proved in Lean. The proofs were produced by an AI system and have not been reviewed by a human.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 1182: f(n) = Θ(n^{3/2} (log n)^{1/2}) and F(n) = Θ(n)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Itaï Ben Yaacov and Arthur Paul Pedersen, "A proof of completeness for continuous first-order logic", Journal of Symbolic Logic 75 (2010) 168–190 (arXiv:0903.4051). Framing: rigorous reconstruction/verification of continuous propositional and first-order syntax/semantics, Group 1 / Group 2 axioms, black-box theorems, and the completeness / approximated strong-completeness results, together with the selected decidability (Corollary 9.11) and compactness (Corollary 9.12) consequences. Project rule: no Lean `axiom` declarations. Itaï Ben Yaacov and Arthur Paul Pedersen did not participate in or endorse this formalization; they have not been contacted about it. Lean is written with AI-agent assistance under Lars Warren Ericson’s direction and review. Mathlib is the Lake dependency. Palomar registration pending; packaging follows the Challenge / Solution / comparator.json pattern. Deviation from the paper: Facts 4.2 and 4.3 (consistency iff satisfiability, Łukasiewicz and continuous propositional logic) needed the added premise that there is at least one propositional variable (`[Nonempty I]`). As literally stated they fail when there are no variables (the empty set is then satisfiable but inconsistent); this counterexample is proved in Lean (`LukPropForm.consistent_iff_satisfiable_fails_empty`, `CLPropForm.consistent_iff_satisfiable_fails_empty`).
entries.title: Ben Yaacov–Pedersen 2010 continuous FOL completeness in Lean 4

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Murat Can Temeller's October 2026 partial result on Erdős Problem #64 (the Erdős–Gyárfás conjecture): every finite simple graph with minimum degree at least 4 and diameter at most 3 contains a cycle of length 4 or 8, and hence a cycle whose length is a power of 2. Five compared theorems state the result with the diameter hypothesis written as pairwise distances at most 3, as G.ediam ≤ 3, and as G.Connected with G.diam ≤ 3 (Mathlib's G.diam is 0 for a disconnected graph), together with the Erdős–Gyárfás form of the conclusion. The proof follows Temeller's argument: assuming no 4-cycle and no 8-cycle, two vertices share at most one neighbour; if every edge lies in a triangle, triangle detours around a fixed vertex force an 8-cycle, and otherwise an edge in no triangle is analysed through bridges, a funnelling step and the short connections forced by the diameter bound, which close a 4-cycle or an 8-cycle in every case.
entries.title: Erdős Problem #64 for minimum degree at least 4 and diameter at most 3

entries.abstract: The Lutz Type 5 triangulation realizes every lattice torus of modulus x+iy with 0 ≤ x ≤ 2⁻³⁶ and 1 ≤ y ≤ 1+2⁻³⁶, including the unit square. The witnesses use a dyadic-grid core with unfolding parameter 1/512 and exact radicals. The proofs verify face lengths, embeddedness, and one-sheeted development to the specified lattice quotient.
entries.title: Dyadic-grid Type 5 origami tori near the square

entries.abstract: For every integer r ≥ 3, the closure in the real line of the ordinary Turán densities of individual finite r-uniform hypergraphs contains a closed interval of positive length. Each forbidden hypergraph has at least one edge. Its density is the limit of the maximum edge count of an n-vertex hypergraph avoiding an injective copy, divided by n choose r. This formalizes Theorem 1.1 of Chen and Liu.
entries.title: Intervals in the closure of the single-hypergraph Turán spectrum

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that both of Tokareva's conjectures on bent functions are false, following Feng, Jiang, Li, Li and Tang (arXiv:2610.32239). The bent-sum conjecture says that, for even n, every Boolean function on 𝔽₂ⁿ of algebraic degree at most n/2 is a sum of two bent functions; the function x₁x₂(x₃x₄ + x₅x₆ + x₇x₈) on 𝔽₂⁸ is a counterexample, and the paper's family gives one in every even dimension n ≥ 8. The derivative conjecture says that every balanced function of degree at most n/2 − 1 with a nonzero period is a derivative g(x) + g(x + a) of a bent function; x₂ + f₈(x₃, …, x₁₀) on 𝔽₂¹⁰ is a counterexample. The proof formalizes the paper's divisibility theorem (if x₁⋯x_k · s is a sum of two bent functions with 2k < n, then 2^(k+1) divides the weight of s), via Fourier inversion and Parseval on 𝔽₂ᵐ, and one direction of Shaporenko's lemma. A separate module proves that x₁x₂ + x₃x₄ + x₅x₆ + x₇x₈ is bent, so the definitions are not vacuous.
entries.title: Counterexamples to Tokareva's conjectures on bent functions

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that Zhi-Wei Sun's conjecture (ii) for OEIS A234360 is false, in the form stated by Formal Conjectures: for n = 1408 there is no 0 < k < n and prime p with (p + k)^2 = (k + 1)^φ(n − k). entries.abstract: Fix any finite list of parities for the numbers of binary ones in columns 1 through K of a Pascal row. Arbitrarily large rows realize this list in any prescribed arithmetic progression. In particular, each positive integer occurs infinitely often in each progression as the first positive column whose binomial coefficient has even binary digit sum (OEIS A249609). A uniform upper bound on a realizing row gives a lower bound of 1/(4 log(1+sqrt(2))) for the liminf of the record divided by log log X in every positive-modulus progression.
entries.title: Finite digit-sum patterns in Pascal rows and record growth for A249609

entries.abstract: Kernel-checked Salem's theorem — every Pisot number is a limit point of Salem numbers from both sides (R. Salem, Algebraic Numbers and Fourier Analysis, D. C. Heath, 1963, Ch. III, Theorem IV, p. 30; origin R. Salem, Duke Math. J. 12 (1945)) — with both of Salem's constructions, each stated as a construction, and (version 2) the rate at which the Salem numbers of the construction approach the Pisot number, with an explicit leading coefficient. Six compared statements. (1) salem_theorem — for a real algebraic integer alpha > 1 every other complex root of whose minimal polynomial has modulus < 1 (the formal-conjectures IsPisot spelling, inlined), and every eps > 0, a Salem number in (alpha - eps, alpha) and one in (alpha, alpha + eps). (2) salem_construction_two_sided — Salem's main construction z^m P(z) ± z^p P(1/z) with its family root in the conclusion, under the nondegeneracy P(1/alpha) != 0 (on the pattern domain strictly stronger than Boyd's proviso "P is not a reciprocal quadratic", with which it coincides when P is the minimal polynomial). (3) salem_quadratic_unit — Salem's second construction, the Chebyshev family for the reciprocal quadratic units, with its family root. These three are version 1's, textually unchanged. (4) pisot_salem_dichotomy — the classical dichotomy behind Salem's definition of the class T (Smyth 2015, Lemma 1, after Salem 1963, p. 26; Hironaka 2006, Section 3.3): a monic, Q-irreducible integer polynomial of degree >= 3 with a real root lambda > 1 and every other complex root in the closed unit disk is reciprocal iff it has a root on the unit circle, and non-reciprocal iff every other root is strictly inside (lambda Pisot); the degree hypothesis cannot be dropped (X^2 - 3X + 1, the smallest member of the reciprocal Pisot family X^2 - aX + 1, a >= 3). (5) salem_rate — under the hypotheses of (2), with P* = P.reverse and e = ±1 the sign of P(1/alpha): P'(alpha) > 0; for every real c, every sequence lambda_n -> alpha of roots of X^n P + c P* satisfies (alpha - lambda_n) alpha^n -> c P*(alpha)/P'(alpha) (the coefficient carries the construction's own sign c, not -c; the limit has the sign of c P(1/alpha)); and for all n >= N the two ladders of Salem's construction exist as Salem roots lambda-_n < alpha of X^n P + e P* (increasing) and lambda+_n > alpha of X^n P - e P* (decreasing), both tending to alpha, with (alpha - lambda-_n) alpha^n -> e P*(alpha)/P'(alpha) > 0 and (alpha - lambda+_n) alpha^n -> -e P*(alpha)/P'(alpha). (6) rate_law — the instance of (5) at P = X^3 - X - 1, c = -1, rho the real root (the smallest Pisot number; Siegel 1944): with coxE m = X^(m-2)(X^3 - X - 1) + (X^3 + X^2 - 1), which is (X - 1) times the Coxeter polynomial of E_m (Gross-Hironaka-McMullen 2009, Cor. 4.3), and lambdaE m the supremum of its real roots > 1: for every m >= 10, lambdaE m is a root of coxE m, lies below rho, is the only real root > 1, and is a Salem number; (rho - lambdaE m) rho^m -> (rho + 1)^2/(3 rho^2 - 1) = 1.2672400139...; and the error ratio (rho - lambdaE (m+1))/(rho - lambdaE m) -> rho^(-1). RESEARCH INTEREST: a quantitative form of Salem's two-sided approximation — a reusable root-perturbation theorem with an explicit leading coefficient, proved along both of Salem's ladders for every pattern polynomial, and applied to the E_m Coxeter family. The mechanism is in print: Hironaka 2006, proof of Theorem 13, p. 507, prints the exact identity behind (5) (exact for t^n P - P*; a factor -1 for t^n P + P*); Boyd-Mossinghoff 2005, p. 412, state geometric convergence of Salem-Boyd sequences and specialize it to x^3 - x - 1 with a leading-term asymptotic (coefficient as retrieved lacking the factor |f*(rho)| = rho^4); McMullen 2002, Theorem 7.4, gives the E_m limit from below. The contribution is the kernel-checked theorem: the rate (5) along both of Salem's ladders for every pattern polynomial, with Boyd's 'for all sufficiently large m' (which version 1 did not state), and its E_m instance (6). The closed constant (rho + 1)^2/(3 rho^2 - 1) was not located as a displayed formula in the classical sources checked; it is, however, the correct coefficient of the Boyd-Mossinghoff asymptotic for the companion branch, and the Oo 2026 preprint tabulates values consistent with it; its priority is not claimed in either direction. Audience: formalized number theory; Mahler measure and Salem/Pisot arithmetic; Coxeter spectral theory. The compared surface uses Mathlib vocabulary and two short definitions made in the Challenge in Mathlib terms (coxE, lambdaE); the statements prove what the definitions are meant to be. NOT formalized: the identification of coxE m with the Coxeter polynomial (cited; kernel-checked in PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005), an explicit onset N in (5) for general P, Boyd's converse, Salem 1944 (S closed), Siegel's minimality of rho, and the equivalence of the Salem-number definitions. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.
entries.title: Salem's theorem: every Pisot number is a two-sided limit of Salem numbers, with the rate of approach

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the Formal Conjectures statement that not every 2-hyperperfect number has the form 3^m(3^(m+1) − 2) with 3^(m+1) − 2 prime. The witness is A. Violette's number N = 3^16 · 129140227 · 256572153302107 · 225205396855537107298933866373 (OEIS A007593). The three large factors are proved prime by Lucas (Pratt) certificates, with all modular powers computed by a verified square-and-multiply function in the kernel. The divisor sum follows from the multiplicativity of σ, and a finite check excludes the special form.
entries.title: A 2-hyperperfect number not of the form 3^m(3^(m+1) − 2)

entries.abstract: No embedded realization of the Lutz Type 2 face complex has all cone angles equal to 2π. Spherical vertex links give strict support and mixed-side witnesses. Lean checks the reduction to determinant signs and a finite propositional refutation.
entries.title: Nonexistence of a Type 2 origami torus

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib disproof of Conjecture 267 of E. DeLaViña's "Written on the Wall II" (a conjecture of the computer program Graffiti.pc, posted Feb. 23, 2007, status O): "If G is a simple connected graph such that girth(G) ≥ 5, then γ_t(G) ≥ CEIL[dist_avg(A,V)], where A is the set of minimum degree vertices." The counterexample is a connected graph on 14 vertices and 16 edges with girth exactly 5 (graph6 M???C@?G?oA_w_A{?). Its unique vertex of minimum degree has distance sum 67 to the other vertices, so ⌈dist_avg(A,V)⌉ = ⌈67/13⌉ = 6, while {3, 6, 11, 12, 13} is a total dominating set, so γ_t(G) = 5. An exhaustive nauty search shows no connected graph of girth at least 5 on at most 13 vertices is a counterexample. The conjecture had already been refuted (with a different, 21-vertex counterexample) by AI Village agents in August 2026; this project contributes the Lean formalization and the smaller counterexample. Because the girth is exactly 5, the disproof holds whether acyclic graphs are given girth 0 (Mathlib's convention, used in the statement) or infinite girth.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 267 is false (a 14-vertex counterexample of girth 5)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Conjecture 377 of E. DeLaViña's "Written on the Wall II" (a conjecture of the computer program Graffiti.pc, posed 18 Feb 2009, status O): every tree T on n > 2 vertices satisfies γ_t(T) ≥ (number of isolates of the subgraph induced by the maximum-degree vertices) + (upper median of the degree sequence). Writing k for the number of isolated maximum-degree vertices, the proof shows γ_t ≥ k + 1 from the edge count of a tree and the bound n ≤ γ_t·Δ, and γ_t ≥ k + 2 when leaves are not a majority (upper median 2), using a Chellali–Haynes type double-counting bound for Δ ≥ 4 and an exact domination count with a short case analysis (ending in 4- or 5-cycles) for Δ = 3.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 377: total domination of trees, isolated maximum-degree vertices and the upper median degree

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Conjecture 380 of E. DeLaViña's "Written on the Wall II" (a conjecture of Graffiti.pc, 18 Feb 2009, status O): for every tree T on n > 2 vertices, γ_t(T) ≥ |D_even(T)| / (ecc(C) − 1), where γ_t is the total domination number, C the centre, ecc(C) the eccentricity of the set C (WOWII definition 52: the largest distance from a vertex outside C to C) and D_even the set of vertices of even degree. The proof establishes the stronger bound γ_t·(ecc(C) − 1) ≥ number of non-leaves whenever ecc(C) ≥ 2 (for ecc(C) ≤ 1, i.e. stars and double stars, the right-hand side is 0 or negative). It combines a double-counting bound 2γ_t ≥ (number of non-leaves) + 2 for a leaf-free minimum total dominating set (the Chellali–Haynes bound) with a short distance argument for ecc(C) = 2.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 380: total domination, even degrees and the eccentricity of the centre of a tree

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 formalization proving the lower bound C1a >= 13/10 = 1.30 for Terence Tao's Optimization Constant 1a (the Sidon-set autocorrelation constant C1a), improving on the previously known lower bounds 1.2748 (Matolcsi-Vinuesa 2010) and 1.292 (Piterbarg-Bajaj-Vincent 2026). The statement surface in Challenge.lean uses only canonical Mathlib and reproduces verbatim the L^2 definition of Constant1a.C1a from FormalConjectures (FormalConjectures/OptimizationConstants/1a.lean, commit 9097e2f90e66). The proof reduces an arbitrary nonnegative square-integrable function to a normalized density supported on [-1/4, 1/4], pairs its autoconvolution and autocorrelation against a 5-tent Bochner-admissible kernel mixture, applies symmetrized smoothing, a 66-mode cosine Bessel lower bound, and weighted Cauchy-Schwarz, and discharges the finite rational sinc^2 lower bounds, the integer Fejer-Riesz sum-of-squares certificate, and the closing quadratic inequalities inside Lean's kernel via decide +kernel using only standard axioms (propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice).
entries.title: Unconditional lower bound C1a >= 13/10 for Tao's Sidon autocorrelation constant

entries.abstract: Let (Ω, μ) be a probability space and a = (aₖ) a family of m square-integrable functions with positive definite Gram matrix I = ∫ a a* dμ. Then for every n ≥ m there are points x₁, …, xₙ ∈ Ω, not necessarily distinct, with (1 − √((m−1)/n))² I ≼ (1/n) ∑ᵢ a(xᵢ) a(xᵢ)* in the Loewner order, that is (1 − √((m−1)/n))² ∫ |f|² dμ ≤ (1/n) ∑ᵢ |f(xᵢ)|² for every f in the span of the family. For bounded measurable functions there are n points with κ ‖f‖_p ≤ m^{1/2−1/p} ((2/n) ∑ᵢ |f(xᵢ)|²)^{1/2} for every 2 ≤ p ≤ ∞ at once, where κ = max(1 − √(m/n), 1/(2m)). This is Proposition 8 of Chkifa, Dolbeault, Krieg and Ullrich, with n points in place of 2n. Up to constants such bounds are due to Bartel, Schäfer and Ullrich, and to Limonova and Temlyakov under a Nikol'skii-type inequality.
entries.title: One-sided discretization of L_p norms with equal weights

entries.abstract: Let f(n) be the least N such that any N points in the plane, no three on a line, contain a convex n-gon. Erdős and Szekeres proved 2^(n-2) + 1 ≤ f(n) ≤ C(2n-4, n-2) + 1 for n ≥ 3. This formalizes both bounds as stated in formal-conjectures (Erdős Problem 107, ersz_bounds). The upper bound comes from Linmiao Xu's formalization; the lower bound construction for all n is new.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 107: the Erdős–Szekeres bounds

entries.abstract: A partial answer to problem 20.52 of the Kourovka Notebook (D. MacHale). For a finite group G of odd order, |G| - k(G) is a multiple of 16, where k(G) is the number of conjugacy classes (Burnside). The problem asks whether every multiple 16m, m > 0, is attained by a non-abelian group of odd order. This formalization proves that it is attained for every odd m and for every m in which 2 occurs to an odd power (m = 2, 6, 8, 10, 14, 18, ...). The groups are (Z/n : Z/3) x Z/a, with Z/3 acting on Z/n by an element u with u^2 + u + 1 = 0, taken with n = 7 and with n = 12 y^2 + 1 for y a power of two. Nothing is proved for m in which 2 occurs to an even power at least 2 (m = 4, 12, 16, 20, ...), so the problem itself stays open.
entries.title: Kourovka problem 20.52, a partial answer: |G| - k(G) = 16m for groups of odd order

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Zakharov's theorem that, for every base g >= 2, the set of natural numbers that are a sum of two base-g palindromes has lower (indeed natural) density zero; this answers Problem 95 of Ben Green's list of 100 open problems in the negative. Two statements of the formal-conjectures file GreensOpenProblems/95.lean are proved: Green95.green_95 (the set of sums of two base-g palindromes, 0 allowed, does not have positive lower density) and Green95.green_95.variants.zakharov (for every g >= 2 there is c > 0 such that, for all large X, the number of n < X that are a sum of two positive base-g palindromes is at most X / (log X)^c). The development proves an explicit exponent c = 1/10 and the density statements for the upper, lower and natural density. The proof uses only the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 95: sums of two palindromes have density zero (Zakharov), in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof that for all gX, gY, gZ > 0, with X ~ N(gX, gX), Y ~ N(gY, gY), Z ~ N(gZ, gZ) and Y, Z independent, neither tanh Y · tanh Z nor tanh X stochastically dominates the other: the c.d.f.s of U = tanh X and V = tanh Y · tanh Z cross on (−1, 1). So the answer to MathOverflow question 505921 (is there gX > 0 with tanh Y tanh Z ⪰_st tanh X?) is no for every gY, gZ > 0. Both laws satisfy the belief-propagation consistency (LLR symmetry) condition; two consistent laws that are stochastically ordered are equal; and the two laws differ near 0 (small-ball masses O(ε) for U, at least of order ε log(1/ε) for V).
entries.title: tanh Y · tanh Z and tanh X are never stochastically ordered for mean = variance Gaussians (a negative answer to MathOverflow 505921)

entries.abstract: Exactly eleven positive nonprimes n satisfy gcd(d²−1,n)>1 for every proper positive divisor d of n. Exactly four of them, 6, 30, 42 and 1722, are midpoints of twin primes. We prove completeness by descent on the largest prime factor and verify the resulting finite tree in Lean.
entries.title: The eleven terms of OEIS A389150

entries.abstract: On an m-dimensional space V of bounded functions on an arbitrary set Ω, and for every ε > 0, there is a finitely supported probability measure ϱ = ∑ₖ wₖ δ(xₖ) for which the uniform norm on V is dominated by the L₂(ϱ) norm with the constant √(m + ε): |f(y)|² ≤ (m + ε) ∑ₖ wₖ |f(xₖ)|² for every y ∈ Ω and every f ∈ V. For continuous functions on a compact domain the same holds with ε = 0. In both cases at most m² + 1 points are needed. The measure is one whose Gram matrix has an almost maximal determinant.
entries.title: The Kiefer–Wolfowitz theorem

entries.abstract: For two finite classical–quantum states, the absolute change in conditional subentropy is bounded by their joint trace distance times the average of κ along the line segment joining their quantum marginals. For distinct states the change is strictly smaller than their joint trace distance. Nevertheless, one is the optimal global Lipschitz constant for every fixed number of labels n ≥ 2 and every quantum dimension m ≥ 1. For n ≥ 2 and any prescribed quantum marginal τ, the optimal constant is κ(τ), the operator norm of the matrix K(τ) in equation (27).
entries.title: Optimal Lipschitz bounds for conditional subentropy

entries.abstract: Leonard Carlitz’s Theorem 1 (1954) determines a signed Euler number modulo an odd prime power p^e when its index is a positive multiple of the totient of p^e. The residue is zero for p congruent to 1 modulo 4 and two for p congruent to 3 modulo 4. We formalize this theorem by a finite alternating-sum argument. For m = 2n−1 and n positive, the reduced numerator a(n) of the Euler polynomial E_m(n) is always divisible by m², and is divisible by m³ exactly when m divides the signed Euler number of index m−1. At odd primes m = p the latter holds exactly when p is congruent to 1 modulo 4. These results prove the conjectures recorded in OEIS A291897 and A292911.
entries.title: Carlitz’s prime-power congruence and cube divisibility in two Euler sequences

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof that for f continuous on [0, ∞), f(0) = 1, f(x) → 0 as x → ∞ and f completely monotone on (0, ∞), the Archimedean copula C(u, v) = f(g(u) + g(v)) (g the inverse of f; C = 0 if u = 0 or v = 0) satisfies C(a, a) − a² ≥ C(u, v) − uv with a = (u + v)/2 for all u, v ∈ [0, 1]. This answers Clark Kimberling's MathOverflow question 195959 (2015), previously settled only for Clayton generators. By Bernstein's theorem each shift f(· + ε) is a Laplace transform; under the normalized measure C(u, v) − uv is a covariance and C(a, a) − a² a variance of exponentials, which a single-crossing (Karlin–Novikoff) argument compares; ε → 0 gives the inequality.
entries.title: Kimberling's inequality C(a, a) − a² ≥ C(u, v) − uv for Archimedean copulas with completely monotone generators (MathOverflow 195959)

entries.abstract: Lagarias and Odlyzko (1985) attack a subset-sum instance (a, M), M = Σ eᵢaᵢ with e ∈ {0,1}ⁿ, by finding a shortest vector of a lattice L(a, M) that contains the planted vector (e, 0). Their Theorem 3.3 proves the planted vector is the shortest one for almost all instances of density below 1/1.54725, just under 1/c₀ ≈ 0.6463107, and they conjectured (§5(2)) that 1/c₀ is the critical density. This project proves the "almost no" half: for every density d > 1/c₀ there is δ > 0 such that, for almost all weights a ∈ [1, ⌊2^{n/d}⌋]ⁿ, no 0/1 vector e of weight at least (1/2 − δ)n makes (e, 0) a shortest nonzero vector of L(a, Σ eᵢaᵢ). The proof is a second-moment count of short integer relations Σ yᵢaᵢ = 0, using a discrete local limit theorem proved from the torus integral and the Dirichlet kernel, and the identification of c₀ with the theta-function saddle point.
entries.title: Lagarias–Odlyzko: the low-density subset-sum attack fails above density 1/c₀

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Ruzsa's 1990 theorem: there is an asymptotic additive basis A of order 2 of the natural numbers whose representation function is bounded in mean square, that is, every large n is a sum of two elements of A, and the number f(n) of ordered representations satisfies sum_{n <= x} f(n)^2 = O(x). This is the case r = 2 of Erdős Problem #1192, which asks the same question for every order r and is open for r >= 3. The statement is the formal-conjectures statement erdos_1192.variants.ruzsa, copied verbatim. The proof is not Ruzsa's. Three parabolas {(x,x^2)}, {(x,-x^2)} and {(x,(2v-1)x^2)} (v a quadratic non-residue) form a basis of order 2 of (Z/p)^2 with additive energy at most 333 p^2. This is lifted to Z/(2p)^2 by a base-2p digit gadget with carry bits, and then to N by placing one block at each of a sequence of geometrically growing scales (primes from Bertrand's postulate). The scales are glued together by a Minkowski inequality for r-fold additive energies, proved by Fourier analysis on Z/N. The development also proves, for every r, that Erdős #1192 at order r is equivalent to the existence of bases of every cyclic group Z/m with r-fold energy at most C m.
entries.title: Ruzsa's just-basis theorem (Erdős Problem #1192, case r = 2)

entries.abstract: Lean 4 disproof of the Equal Halves conjecture of L. Gillibert (2026): every finite connected vertex-transitive graph of even order would have a partition V = A ⊔ B into nonempty sets with G[A] and G[B] connected and isomorphic (induced subgraphs). The counterexample is graph 2659 of the Holt–Royle census of vertex-transitive graphs on 28 vertices (9-regular, automorphism group of order 504, not a Cayley graph). The kernel checks that for no vertex set A are G[A] and G[Aᶜ] isomorphic: an isomorphism would give an involution preserving same-side degree, triangle and distance-two counts, and 15 tests on these statistics, evaluated on all 2-colourings up to the stabiliser of a vertex, rule this out.
entries.title: Gillibert's Equal Halves conjecture is false (a non-Cayley vertex-transitive graph on 28 vertices)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 disproof of Written on the Wall II Conjecture 72 of Graffiti.pc, which asserts tree(G) ≥ ⌈ecc_avg(G) + max_v λ(v)/3⌉ for every finite simple connected graph G, where tree(G) is the order of a largest induced tree, ecc_avg(G) the average eccentricity and λ(v) the independence number of the neighbourhood of v. The counterexample has 19 vertices: two 4-cycles through a common vertex, one of whose far vertices is replaced by a clique of 13 twins. Its eccentricities sum to 70, max_v λ(v) = 4 and tree(G) = 5, so the bound would be ⌈70/19 + 4/3⌉ = 6. The statement is the negation of the Formal Conjectures statement.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 72 is false (a 19-vertex counterexample)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the exact characterization "a real exponent c is valid in Ben Green's Open Problem 19 if and only if c >= 4", hence C = 4. Valid means: there is an absolute K > 0 such that for every density alpha in (0,1) and every sufficiently large n, every subset A of F_2^n x F_2^n of density at least alpha has a nonzero d for which the set of corners (x,y), (x+d,y), (x,y+d) in A has at least K alpha^c N^2 elements, N = 2^n. The upper bound (c = 4 is valid) formalizes Mandache's regularity argument on F_2^n with a finite weighted triforce inequality; the lower bound (no c < 4 is valid) formalizes the Behrend / Ruzsa-Szemeredi construction with random labellings and finite-product concentration. The proof uses only the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 19: the popular-corner exponent C = 4 in F_2^n x F_2^n, in Lean 4

entries.abstract:
For m≥1 complex fields, add one real trilinear term per unordered triple of distinct fields to Σᵢ Re(zᵢ³). If the resulting cubic’s real gradient norm depends only on |z|, then m is 1, 4 or 13. Both larger cases occur. Up to real isometry for the trace metric, their cubics are √6 times the trace of the Jordan cube on traceless Hermitian 3×3 matrices over ℂ and the octonions, respectively.

For a finite-dimensional real Euclidean cubic W(x)=d(x,x,x) with symmetric trilinear form d, define ⟨x∘y,z⟩=d(x,y,z). Assume the eikonal law |x∘x|²=c|x|⁴ with c>0. Every orthogonal decomposition into at least two nonzero product-closed subspaces consists of four lines, four planes, thirteen planes, or nine planes and an eight-dimensional block. Each pattern occurs at c=1.

For an orthogonal decomposition of such an eikonal cubic into three or more closed planes, a triple’s share is ½tr(PQ), where P and Q project orthogonally onto the third plane and the span of products from the first two, respectively. Shares lie in [0,1]. For each pair the remaining shares sum to two. For thirteen planes at least 52 unordered triples have positive share.

For triples of pairwise unbiased orthonormal bases of ℍ³, the planes spanned by their rank-one projectors centered at I/3 have minimum share 1−1/√3. Every pairwise unbiased family has at most five bases. In the Albert algebra of Hermitian 3×3 octonionic matrices, twelve pairwise unbiased Jordan frames have a thirteenth unbiased to all, unique up to ordering its idempotents. Systems of thirteen pairwise unbiased Albert frames with exactly 52 unordered triples of positive trace share exist and form one orbit under Jordan automorphisms and relabelling of the frames and of their idempotents.

Compare cubics of equal eikonal strength c, each decomposed into at least two orthogonal closed planes. Scaling mixed terms by t gives Wₜ with energy |∇Wₜ|²/(9c). On a common decomposition, energy on every three-plane sum determines t and, for t∉{0,1}, W and Wₜ up to one sign. At t=0 or t=1, another eikonal cubic of the same strength on the same plane system gives identical energy everywhere at t, and its scaled cubic lies outside {Wₜ, −Wₜ}. If both parameters are positive and differ from one, equal energies everywhere identify the planes up to permutation.

This Lean development accompanies the paper of the same title, which is available at https://github.com/macgregor-sudo/cartan-cubic-planes/releases/tag/v1.0.0 and has been submitted to Hexagon. The README states all thirteen compared theorems and lists further results.
entries.title: On the planes of Cartan's cubics and the missing seven

entries.abstract: The first machine-checked proof of Feige's conjecture in its GENERAL-δ form (previous Lean work, LeanPool's Feige/, covers only δ = 1). The mathematics follows Ling's proof (arXiv:2608.18392); the formalization also proves two steps the paper leaves unproved (Claim 3.4 and the minimisation over m in Corollary 1.3). Lean 4 proofs of (1) Feige's conjecture in its general form: for independent, nonnegative, integrable X₁, …, Xₙ with E[Xᵢ] ≤ μ (μ > 0) and every δ > 0, P(∑ Xᵢ − E[∑ Xᵢ] < δμ) ≥ min(δ/(1+δ), e⁻¹); and (2) the lower-bound half of Samuels' conjecture (Ling's Theorem 1.1): for ordered means 0 ≤ m₁ ≤ … ≤ mₙ, λ > ∑ mᵢ and independent nonnegative Xᵢ with E[Xᵢ] = mᵢ, P(∑ Xᵢ < λ) ≥ minᵢ ∏_{j ≥ i} (1 − mⱼ/(λ − ∑_{k<i} mₖ)). The proofs follow Z. Ling, On Samuels' Conjecture (arXiv:2608.18392): a two-point mixture decomposition (vendored from LeanPool), Bernoullification and a Bellman-type induction on weighted Bernoulli sums. The sharpness and attainment half of Ling's Theorem 1.1 is not formalized.
entries.title: Feige's inequality for every δ > 0 (sharp constant min(δ/(1+δ), e⁻¹)) and the lower bound in Samuels' conjecture, following Ling's proof

entries.abstract: A two-sided class-gap rate and an explicit smooth common-profile upper witness for the scalar two-layer scan on normalized Euclidean round area.
entries.title: Matching round-area rates for null-clock scans with hidden focusing

entries.abstract: Every finite quitting game whose singleton prizes lie in an affine plane has a uniform Nash equilibrium payoff under independent randomization. One profile per tolerance works at every sufficiently large horizon against arbitrary unilateral behavioral deviations.
entries.title: Uniform equilibrium in planar quitting games

entries.abstract: For integers k ≥ 2, offsets 0 = r_0 < r_1 < ... < r_k = w with d = gcd(r_1, ..., r_k), and n > 0 with gcd(n, d) = 1, let H_λ be the numerical semigroup generated by n + λw + r_i (0 ≤ i ≤ k). With PF(H) the pseudo-Frobenius numbers, tr(H) = {h ∈ H : ∃ p ∈ PF(H), ∀ f ∈ PF(H), h + p - f ∈ H} and res(H) = |H \ tr(H)|, the record states that there are integers A ≥ 0, B and L ≥ 0 with res(H_λ) = Aλ + B for every integer λ ≥ L (PROOF.md §7 Theorem).
entries.title: Eventual affine trace residue in shifted numerical semigroups

entries.abstract:
Can the same two localized wave patterns occur arbitrarily many times in one infinite network, without spreading into the rest of it? For the specific octagonal Ammann–Beenker graph studied here, the answer is yes.

The network is built by projecting selected points of a four-dimensional integer lattice into the plane. Its graph Laplacian L assigns the same weight, 1/16, to each edge. Two known compact wave patterns, A and B, live on separate eight-site rings of a central seventeen-vertex patch. Their amplitudes alternate between +1 and −1 and vanish elsewhere. They have exact eigenvalues 3/16 and 1/4, respectively.

The new theorem proves that for any finite number N, we can find N copies of this patch arbitrarily far from the origin and farther apart than any prescribed separation. The copies include the complete surrounding candidate neighborhoods, with both present and absent vertices preserved. These neighborhoods do not overlap. This is possible because certain lattice translations move arbitrarily far in physical space while their displacement in the internal projection tends to zero.

Each copy carries the same two localized waves, with exactly the original amplitudes and eigenvalues. The eigenvector equations hold at every vertex of the infinite graph, even outside the patch, where the contributions cancel. Every copied wave has squared norm eight. The two waves in each copy, and all waves in different copies, are mutually orthogonal. Thus the construction gives 2N nonzero, mutually orthogonal compact eigenvectors on a single infinite graph. No artificial boundary, numerical approximation or global translation symmetry is assumed.

Why is this interesting? The earlier results established an isolated two-state system at one location. The new result proves that its underlying compact wave patterns can be replicated at arbitrarily many separated locations, providing a geometric and spectral foundation for placing local two-state systems on the same network. It does not yet make them degenerate, individually isolated or independently controllable qubits: the two Laplacian eigenvalues differ. Engineering distinct degenerate rest energies, proving spectral isolation and implementing local control are the next research goals.

Repetitivity of cut-and-project sets and compact localized states are established research topics. This result certifies their concrete combination for the specified graph and Laplacian, not a claim of priority or experimental feasibility. The full 129-module Lean/Mathlib library passed verification, and all 16 selected propositions passed independent comparison using the Lean default, NanoDa and con-ron kernels. No Palomar registration or independent human peer review is claimed for this seventh candidate.
entries.title: Exact Recurrence and Spatial Replication of Compact Localized Eigenstates on an Infinite Ammann–Beenker Graph

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof that Friedan's entropy inequality holds without the assumption that the Hamiltonians commute, answering the quantum question of MathOverflow 138395: for Hermitian n × n matrices H₀, H₁ and 0 ≤ a ≤ 1, with Gibbs states ρ_H = e^{−H}/Z(H), von Neumann entropies S(H), H_a = (1 − a)H₀ + aH₁ and K = Z(H_a)/(Z(H₀)^{1−a} Z(H₁)^a), K² S(H_a) ≤ (1 − a) S(H₀) + a S(H₁). Also proved: the same for m Hamiltonians, and a S(ρ) + (1 − a) S(σ) ≥ K² S(M/K), K = tr M, for the log-Euclidean mean of m faithful states, the α-z means (positive semidefinite states, any z > 0), the Kubo–Ando mean and the multivariate product means. The proof bounds the spectrum of the mean by weak log-majorization (Ky Fan, Horn, Ando–Hiai), shows that g(x) = (Σ eˣⁱ)² H(softmax x) is increasing and Schur-convex, and reduces to the classical inequality at the aligned commuting pair.
entries.title: Friedan's entropy inequality for non-commuting Hamiltonians (the quantum question of MathOverflow 138395), for m Hamiltonians and for other matrix geometric means

entries.abstract: Krenn, Gu and Zeilinger (Physical Review Letters 119, 240403, 2017) showed that an experiment built from probabilistic photon-pair sources and linear optics corresponds to an edge-weighted graph: vertices are output paths, edges are pair sources, the colour at each end of an edge is the mode of the photon sent to that path, and each perfect matching is one way for every detector to click. A matching gives every vertex the colour of its edge at that vertex, the "inherited vertex colouring" of Krenn's problem statement, and the amplitude of a vertex colouring is the sum, over the perfect matchings inheriting it, of the product of their complex edge weights. Gu, Erhard, Zeilinger and Krenn (PNAS 116, 4147, 2019) develop this weighted interference picture. The experiment produces a D-dimensional GHZ state on N photons exactly when each of the D constant colourings has amplitude 1 and every other colouring has amplitude 0. Krenn, Gu and Soltész ask whether such a graph exists (arXiv:1902.06023, Question 1); the conjecture, known as the Krenn–Gu conjecture, is that it does not once N ≥ 6 and D ≥ 3. For N = 4 a solution with D = 3 does exist, given by the three perfect matchings of K_4, which is why the conjecture starts at six vertices. This formalisation proves the conjecture in full: for every even N ≥ 6 and every D ≥ 3, no assignment of complex weights to the endpoint-coloured edges of K_N satisfies these equations. This is the normalised condition of Chandran, Gajjala and Illickan (MFCS 2024, Sections 1.1 and 1.4), who proved the conjecture when the underlying graph has vertex connectivity at most two or maximum degree at most three; Cervera-Lierta, Krenn and Aspuru-Guzik (Quantum 6, 836, 2022) had excluded the cases (N, D) = (6, 3) and (8, 4) for edges with equal endpoint colours. Here the weights are arbitrary complex numbers and the two ends of an edge may carry different colours; no sparsity, positivity or symmetry is assumed, and a weight on K_N stands for the total weight of any parallel edges with the same endpoint colours. Physically, photon-pair sources and linear optics without further resources cannot produce a GHZ state of local dimension three or more on six or more photons. The Lean statement `MonochromaticQuantumGraph.eqSystem_no_solution_ge6_ge3` and its definitions are those of the Formal Conjectures file `FormalConjectures/Paper/MonochromaticQuantumGraph.lean`. The proof shows that the equations force every edge with nonzero weight to have equal endpoint colours and each colour class to be a single perfect matching, and then applies Bogdanov's obstruction for three such matchings. It uses only the axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
entries.title: Krenn–Gu conjecture on monochromatic quantum graphs: no complex solution for even N ≥ 6 and D ≥ 3

entries.abstract: A pure-Init Lean 4.35.0 formalization (zero Mathlib dependencies, zero SAT certificates) disproving the Section 5 conjecture of Fanelli and Moscardelli (ECAI 2025, hal-05368668; google-deepmind/formal-conjectures FanelliMoscardelli.stability_threshold_tight). Proves via an elementary 9-lemma structural proof that for every integer m >= 3, every complete strict preference profile on N = 2m + 1 agents admits an m-stable matching, giving K(2m + 1) <= m < ceil((2m + 1)/2) and refuting stability_threshold_tight using only the three standard Lean axioms [propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice].
entries.title: Disproof of the Fanelli–Moscardelli Conjecture on Approximate Stable Roommates in Lean 4

entries.abstract: The sequence starts with three ones and adds the gcd of its current term and its term two places earlier. A finite modular invariant confines its positive jumps to a set of 34 integers and excludes 14. This disproves the assertion that every positive integer occurs as a difference.
entries.title: Disproof of the Jump Universality Conjecture for OEIS A260194

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof of the inequality asked about by Daniel Friedan on MathOverflow 138395: for probability vectors X, Y on n points, 0 ≤ α ≤ 1, zᵢ = Xᵢ^α Yᵢ^{1−α}, K = Σ zᵢ > 0 and Z = z/K, the Shannon entropies satisfy K² H(Z) ≤ α H(X) + (1 − α) H(Y). Also proved: Theorem M, the same inequality for m distributions with weights summing to 1 (zᵢ = ∏ⱼ Xⱼ(i)^{aⱼ}), and Theorem R2, the Rényi-entropy version on two points for every order 0 < γ ≤ 2 log 2, γ ≠ 1, and every m. The two-distribution proof is a descent on the size of the support with concavity arguments for four or more, three and two atoms; Theorem M follows by an index lemma for the Hessian of (Σ eˣⁱ)² H(softmax x) and a maximum principle on faces of the weight simplex.
entries.title: Friedan's generalized entropy inequality α H(X) + (1 − α) H(Y) ≥ K² H(Z) for all n and α (MathOverflow 138395), for m distributions, and its two-point Rényi version

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 disproof of Erdős Problem 549 in the form stated by Formal Conjectures: it is not true that every tree T with k vertices in one class and 2k in the other has diagonal Ramsey number R(T) = 4k − 1. The witness is k = 4 and the double star S(3,7), whose centres have 3 and 7 leaves, with classes of sizes 4 and 8. An explicit 2-colouring of the edges of K₁₅ contains no monochromatic copy, so R(T) ≥ 16 > 15. The colouring is checked by the Lean kernel.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 549 is false: a double star with R(T) > 4k − 1 at k = 4

entries.abstract: The complete k-partite graph K_{2,...,2} is k-choosable (Erdős, Rubin and Taylor 1979). It is a case of Ohba's conjecture (2002) that ch(G) = χ(G) whenever G has at most 2χ(G)+1 vertices, which Noel, Reed and Wu proved in 2015. This package formalizes only the Erdős–Rubin–Taylor case, by a direct induction with Hall's theorem. The analogous question for parts of size three is harder: ch(K_{3*k}) = ⌈(4k−1)/3⌉ (Kierstead 2000).
entries.title: Erdős–Rubin–Taylor: complete multipartite graphs with parts of size 2 are k-choosable

entries.abstract: The join of q >= 1 disjoint copies of an odd cycle C_m (m >= 3) is 3q-critical: its chromatic number is 3q, and deleting any vertex or any edge lowers it. This gives three classical lower bounds. Dirac: f_6(4n+2) >= 4n^2+8n+3 for n >= 1 (Erdős Problem 917). Erdős: if k >= 3 and 3 | k, then f_k(n) >= ½(1 − 1/(k/3))n^2 + n for every n = m·k/3 with m odd and m >= 3 (Erdős Problem 917). Dirac: for infinitely many n there is a 6-critical graph on n vertices with minimum degree > n/2 (Erdős Problem 1032). Here f_k(n) is the largest number of edges of a k-critical graph on n vertices, and k-critical means both vertex- and edge-critical.
entries.title: Dirac's joins of odd cycles: Erdős Problems 917 (Dirac, Erdős 3 | k) and 1032 (Dirac 6-critical)

entries.abstract: For a graph G and integer n, let h_G(n) be the maximum over all n-vertex induced subgraphs of the minimum number of edge deletions needed to make the subgraph bipartite. Erdős, Hajnal, and Szemerédi (1982) constructed a graph G with chromatic number aleph_1 and h_G(n) <= 2 n^(3/2), and Erdős (1981) conjectured that for every ε > 0 there exists a graph G with chromatic number aleph_1 and h_G(n) = O(n^(1+ε)). This package gives an original ZFC machine-checked proof of Erdős's conjecture.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 111: Uncountably chromatic graphs with bipartite distance O(n^(1+ε))

entries.abstract: The exact Coxeter-polynomial formula for the star trees T(p,q,r) and the convergence of their spectral radii as one arm grows. The three arms have p, q, r nodes, each counted WITH the centre, so E_m = T(2,3,m-3) and D_n = T(2,2,n-2). With [m] = 1 + X + ... + X^(m-1) and F_{p,q} = X^(p+q-2) - [p-1][q-1], five compared theorems: (1) for all p, q, r >= 2, with the generalized Cartan matrix given entrywise and the Coxeter element the ordered product of the reflections 1 - e_i e_i^T A of the geometric representation, (X - 1) * charpoly(c) = X^(r+1) F_{p,q} - F*_{p,q}, F* the reversal (Polynomial.reverse); (2) for (p,q) != (2,2), F_{p,q} has exactly one real root L(p,q) > 1, and L(p,q) < 2; (3) for (p,q) != (2,2) there are r0 >= 2 and lambda_r, the largest real eigenvalue of the Coxeter element of T(p,q,r) for r >= r0, with lambda_r in (1, L), every complex characteristic root z satisfying norm(z) <= lambda_r, strict increase in r, and convergence to L(p,q); thus these lambda_r are the Coxeter spectral radii; (4) for tau > 0, F_{p,q}(tau) = 0 if and only if (tau^-1 + ... + tau^-(p-1)) (tau^-1 + ... + tau^-(q-1)) = 1, the equation of the growth rate of the triangle Coxeter group (p,q,inf) (kernel-held in PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000013; only the equivalence of the two equations is proved here); (5) for rho the real root of x^3 = x + 1, rho <= L(p,q), with equality exactly at (p,q) = (2,3) and (3,2). These are classical results about Coxeter transformations and spectral limits of trees, relevant to Coxeter groups, spectral graph theory, and the study of Salem and Pisot limits. The all-parameter formula and one-arm spectral limit are main subjects of Evripidou's paper; this package treats its three-arm i = 0 family, extending the previously formalized E_m sequence to each fixed (p,q). Statements (2), (4) and (5) characterize and compare those limits. Through (4), (2) and (5) restate results of PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000013; that overlap is disclosed. No mathematical novelty or formalization priority is claimed. The compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary (Matrix.charpoly, Matrix.diagonal, List.finRange / List.prod, Finset.range and Finset.Icc sums, Polynomial.reverse, Polynomial.map, Polynomial.eval, Filter.Tendsto, nhds) — zero custom definitions on the compared surface.
entries.title: Coxeter polynomials and spectral-radius limits of three-arm star trees

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 formalization of two explicit, strictly increasing, pairwise disjoint infinite families x(m) and y(m) (m >= 0) of base-6 Lychrel numbers under repeated base-6 reverse-and-add T(n) = n + rev_6(n). Family 1 has 110 + 2m base-6 digits (smallest seed x(0) with 86 decimal digits) and Family 2 has 108 + 2m base-6 digits (smallest seed y(0) with 84 decimal digits), with middle blocks linked by base-6 digit complement d |-> 5 - d. Both satisfy the exact period-12 self-similar recurrence T^[12](x(m)) = x(m + 3) and T^[12](y(m)) = y(m + 3) while avoiding all base-6 palindromes, proving unconditionally that infinitely many base-6 Lychrel numbers exist. Coverage by this package's Palomar comparison: of the companion paper's 10 main results, 2 are compared in Lean in full (20%; Theorems 1 and 2) and 2 in part (Corollary 3: every x(m) and y(m) is a base-6 Lychrel number, without its positivity and per-iterate form; Theorem 7: the two families are disjoint, without the injectivity of all six forward trajectories); 5 more (Lemma 4, Theorem 5, Proposition 6, Theorem 8 and Corollary 9) are proved in this package's Lean library but not compared, though the compared statements include the infinitude of base-6 Lychrel numbers; Proposition 10 is by certificate only; Conjecture 11 is open and not counted.
entries.title: Two infinite families of base-6 Lychrel numbers

entries.abstract: Standalone, zero-dependency Lean 4 (v4.36.0) formalization proving an unconditional finite-graph improvement on Balogh–Clemen–Lidický Conjecture 1.4 (European Journal of Combinatorics 121, 2024, Paper No. 103841, arXiv:2203.15764): for every rational density alpha = p/q in [63/100, 1] and every finite simple triangle-free graph G on n >= 100,000 vertices, there exists a vertex subset A of exact size floor(alpha * n) such that e(A) + e(A^c) <= ((2*alpha - 1) / 4) * n^2, with zero + o(n^2) asymptotic error term. This lowers the published threshold from alpha >= 0.717 down to alpha >= 63/100 = 0.63, closing 66.3% of the open conjecture gap [2 - sqrt(2), 0.717]. The proof combines exact integer 2-partition concavity rounding, a vertex-transfer monotonicity lemma, a single rank-2 5x5 integer sum-of-squares certificate verified over all 388/1,024 labeled triangle-free 5-graphs by pure kernel decide, a 3-line global sum-of-squares proof for alpha >= 2 - sqrt(7)/2 (approx 0.6771), and exact 2D/3D homogeneous Bernstein binary-tree certificates (510 leaves, 36 pruned nodes), compiled entirely inside the Lean 4 kernel with zero external dependencies, zero sorry, zero native_decide, and only standard Lean axioms.
entries.title: Balogh–Clemen–Lidický Conjecture 1.4: Unbalanced 2-Partitions of Triangle-Free Graphs (alpha >= 63/100)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Zalcman coefficient inequality for all sufficiently large indices, with equality precisely at Koebe rotations. A single threshold works for the entire normalized univalent class.
entries.title: The Zalcman inequality for sufficiently large indices

entries.abstract: Which roots of the Coxeter polynomial are algebraic conjugates of the Salem spectral radius, and which are roots of unity? For every E_m star tree of rank m >= 10, the three new compared theorems (23)-(25) answer this question for the explicit Coxeter matrix. The seven possible orders 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 18, 30 are selected by rank congruences. Dividing out one copy of each selected cyclotomic polynomial gives exactly the minimal polynomial of the spectral radius over Q. In particular, it has the full degree m precisely for m = 2, 10, 16, 20, 22, 26 or 28 modulo 30. This formalizes Gross-Hironaka-McMullen, Theorem 1.1 in the hyperbolic range and Corollary 1.4. The proof uses cyclotomic conjugacies and the simple-root count for the Salem family. For example, rank 38 gives the factor Phi_30 and a Salem number of degree 30. This version also includes all 22 version-2 statements on the degree-12 compositum of the cubic and quartic Mahler minimizers, its exact Mahler measure and minimal recurrence, the Bedford-Kim plastic family, Lehmer's polynomial and the Coxeter bridge.
entries.title: Mahler minimizers and the Salem factors of the E_m Coxeter polynomials

entries.abstract: A Lean proof of the finite question of Segal recorded as a variant of Erdős problem 473. For each n at least two, the integers from one through n have a permutation in which consecutive entries sum to a prime.
entries.title: Prime-sum permutations of the integers from 1 to n

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Written on the Wall II Conjecture 372 of Graffiti.pc on its defined domain: every finite tree T on more than two vertices with path cover number p(T) ≥ 2 satisfies γ_t(T) ≥ τ(T) / (p(T) − 1), where γ_t is the total domination number and τ the vertex cover number. Two variants are also proved: τ(T) ≤ γ_t(T) for trees of order at least two that are covered by at most two disjoint paths, and τ(T) ≤ γ_t(T) · max(1, p(T) − 1) for every tree of order at least two. The statements are those of the Formal Conjectures repository.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 372: total domination, vertex covers and path covers of trees

entries.abstract: In a balanced stable-marriage market of size n, each participant independently chooses a uniformly random strict ranking. Write S_n for the number of stable complete matchings. For absolute constants C and t_0 greater than zero and every fixed 0 < t < t_0, the limit superior as n tends to infinity of Pr(S_n <= t n log n) is at most C t^2 log(e/t). Bo Cowgill and Will Cook are coauthors of this fixed-threshold result.
entries.title: A quantitative lower-tail bound for random stable matchings

entries.abstract: A complete, elementary Lean 4 proof that every convex set in R^3 has additive VC_2-dimension at most 2, settling the open conjecture VCDimConvex.hasAddVCNDimAtMost_two_two_of_convex_r3 from Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures repository. Combined with Kenta Kitamura's 2x2 lower bound, this determines the exact value VC_2(convex sets in R^3) = 2 (improving the previous finite upper bound of 2^128 - 1). The proof uses no topology, no Hahn-Banach theorem, and no closedness assumptions on C: it shows no coplanar 2x3 grid is in convex position, reduces any non-degenerate 3x3 grid via an explicit invertible affine map to paraboloid normal form, and derives a 4-point convex combination contradiction from just two 7-point masks.
entries.title: Additive VC_2 Dimension of Convex Sets in R^3

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof that for every n ≥ 3 the set of node sets -1 ≤ x₁ < … < xₙ ≤ 1 with minimal Lebesgue constant is uncountable (Rack and Vajda 2015, Theorem 2.5). The proof shows that a minimiser exists (continuity, compactness and blow-up of the Lebesgue constant as nodes collide), rescales it to a canonical minimiser, and shrinks it slightly.
entries.title: Optimal interpolation nodes are not unique for n ≥ 3 (Erdős Problem 1129, variant)

entries.abstract: For positive integers k and p, among finite simple connected graphs with distance-k packing number p, the maximum sum of the six pairwise shortest distances on four distinct vertices is 6k + 4(k+1)(p−1). A distance-k packing requires all its pairwise distances to exceed k. More generally, for nonnegative integer terminal weights the maximum product-weighted sum is k times the total weight of the six pairs plus (k+1)(p−1) times the maximum weighted cut on the four terminals. Both endpoints prove the universal bound and construct an attaining connected graph with exact packing number p.
entries.title: Sharp distance packing for four prescribed terminals

entries.abstract: The exponential generating function A(x) of OEIS A368630 satisfies A(0) = 1 and A(x/A(x)^2) = exp(x A(x)). The package proves that this equation determines a unique integer coefficient sequence, and that a(n) ≡ 1 (mod 3) for every n, a(2n) is odd for every n, and a(2n+1) is even for n ≥ 1, as conjectured by Paul D. Hanna (OEIS A368630, 2024).
entries.title: OEIS A368630: three congruences (Hanna's conjectures)

entries.abstract: For a prime p, B(n + (p^p − 1)/(p − 1)) ≡ B(n) (mod p) (Touchard 1933, Hall 1934, Williams 1945). The periods conjectured by G. C. Greubel in OEIS A146107, A146109, A146113, A146119 and A146121 (p = 17, 19, 23, 29, 31) are instances; OEIS already marks them correct. Minimality is not claimed.
entries.title: Bell numbers modulo a prime are periodic with period (p^p−1)/(p−1) (Touchard, Hall)

entries.abstract: For every fixed ζ, ε > 0, a finite simple graph of sufficiently large degree bound Δ and maximum pair codegree at most ζΔ has list chromatic number at most (ζ + ε)Δ. The degree threshold is uniform in the number of vertices and in the lists.
entries.title: A proof of Vu’s conjecture

entries.abstract: Pure core Lean 4 (zero Mathlib imports) formalization answering Padrol–Philippe (Combinatorica 44, 2024) Question 7.21 in the negative in every VC-dimension rank r >= 4 via window sweep acycloids W(n, m). Alongside the counterexample family (for 3 <= m <= n/2, starting at W(6, 3) with 240 permutations and rank 4), the compared theorems establish exact cardinality and simple allowable/sweep-acycloid structure, the full shattered-forest characterization and VC dimension, failure of matroid augmentation, three independent non-matroidal obstructions (oriented-matroid minor contraction, a da Silva potential-sweep witness, and the Knauer–Marc excluded partial-cube minor Q_{n - 2m + 4}^{--}(n - 2m + 4) together with Tamura's C_0 match at W(6, 3)), and exact realizability for m <= 2 over every linearly ordered commutative ring with 0 < 1. Main results: 14 of 14 in Lean (100%) · Abstract claims: 14 of 14 in Lean (100%) · 2 supporting lemmas (16 of 16 numbered claims compared in Challenge.lean, 72 of 72 verified declarations in Verify.lean; zero sorry, zero native_decide, standard axioms only). Uses the tope reading of Padrol–Philippe Definition 7.13(i) (extension to all covectors cited from Section 7.4 and Lemma 7.17). Rank 3 remains open. Companion page: https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/sweep-acycloids-not-oriented-matroids.
entries.title: Window Sweep Acycloids W(n, m) Answer Padrol–Philippe Question 7.21 in Every Rank r >= 4

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof of Erdős's 1947 theorem that for any n ≥ 2 distinct interpolation nodes in [-1, 1] the smallest of the n + 1 local maxima of the Lebesgue function Σ|ℓₖ| (over the gaps between consecutive nodes and the endpoints ±1) is less than √n.
entries.title: Erdős's bound Υ(x) < √n for the Lebesgue function of interpolation nodes (Erdős Problem 1130, variant)

entries.abstract: One 1,856-period calendar of independently randomized moves is an exact terminal Nash equilibrium and a uniform Cesàro equilibrium in the four-player quitting game for every live phase.
entries.title: Periodic equilibrium in Simon’s four-player quitting game

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof of Gisin's theorem for two finite-dimensional systems of any dimensions: a pure state violates the CHSH inequality, for some choice of +/-1-valued observables on each side, if and only if it is not a product state. A vector of the joint system is a function psi : m x n -> C on a product basis, an observable is a Hermitian involution, the correlation of A and B is <psi, (A (x) B) psi> with Mathlib's Kronecker product, and the CHSH expression is <A0 B0> + <A0 B1> + <A1 B0> - <A1 B1>. Also proved separately: a unit product vector satisfies |CHSH| <= 2 for all such observables. The proof of the violation splits off two Schmidt terms of a non-product vector without a full singular value decomposition, from two eigenvectors of Psi Psi^H with positive eigenvalues, measures Z and X on Alice's two-dimensional span and cZ +/- tX on Bob's, with c and t chosen from the two Schmidt coefficients sigma0, sigma1, and acts as the identity on the orthogonal complements; the rest of the vector then contributes exactly its squared norm times 2, and the total is 2 + 2(sqrt(N^2 + C^2) - N) > 2, where N = sigma0^2 + sigma1^2 and C = 2 sigma0 sigma1 > 0. Controls exercise a product vector, the Bell state, a weakly entangled two-qubit state and a 3 x 3 state with three Schmidt terms.
entries.title: Gisin's theorem for two finite-dimensional systems

entries.abstract: Two diamonds joined at tips by a path with three new vertices disprove the proposed universal inequality between the second-largest adjacency eigenvalue and the largest Laplacian eigenvalue minus two.
entries.title: Counterexample to Cazenave's second spectral graph conjecture

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof of the Erdős–Rado theorem that every red/blue colouring of the 3-element subsets of the reals, ordered as usual, has either a red set of order type ω + n or a blue set of four reals, for every finite n ≥ 2 (the partition relation 𝔠 → (ω + n, 4)³ of Erdős and Rado, 1956, Theorem 31). It is a positive partial answer to Erdős Problem 70. The development includes infinite Ramsey theorems for pairs and triples on ℕ and lemmas on uncountable sets of reals.
entries.title: Erdős–Rado partition relation 𝔠 → (ω + n, 4)³ for the real line (Erdős Problem 70, variant)

entries.abstract:
Can two exactly localized states remain isolated in energy if the potential stops growing away from their center? For the specific infinite Ammann–Beenker graph studied here, the answer is yes. This result replaces the growing radial potential of the earlier theorems with a bounded potential that is constant far from the origin, while retaining the exact two-state degeneracy and a positive certified rest-energy gap.

The graph is defined by projecting admitted points of a four-dimensional integer lattice into the plane, using an octagonal acceptance window. Edges join admitted lattice points differing by a signed coordinate unit vector. The interaction L is the positive graph Laplacian with edge weight 1/16, acting on the real square-summable states of the entire infinite graph. No finite sample or artificial boundary is introduced.

The original onsite potential 1 + r², where r is the distance from the origin, is now truncated to V(r) = min(1 + r², C), with C = 4 + 2√2 (approximately 6.828). A fixed onsite correction of 17/16 + √2 is retained on the eight vertices of the first ring. The resulting Hamiltonian is a bounded self-adjoint operator defined on the whole real Hilbert space. Outside the seventeen vertices of the central sector, the onsite value is exactly C.

Two compact states, A and B, have alternating amplitudes +1 and −1 on their respective eight-site rings and vanish everywhere else. They are orthogonal, each has squared norm eight, and both are exact eigenvectors at E* = 13/4 + √2 (approximately 4.664). The theorem proves that the entire eigenspace at E* has dimension exactly two: every state at that energy is a linear combination of A and B. Moreover, every other energy in the full real spectrum lies at distance at least 1/122 from E*. This excludes not only other eigenvalues but also any non-discrete real spectral energies within the open protected window. The radius is a rigorous lower bound, not a claimed exact gap.

There is a useful comparison with the uniform reference operator C I + L, called the bulk here. Its entire real spectrum lies in [C, C + 1], strictly above E*. The actual Hamiltonian differs from this reference only by a perturbation supported on the central sector, whose range has dimension at most seventeen. The enclosure does not say that the bulk fills the interval or that the full Hamiltonian has no other levels below it.

Why is this interesting? Localized states in an infinite network need not depend on confinement throughout the network. Here a strictly local modification of a uniform background produces an exactly two-dimensional isolated energy space, with a quantitative guarantee valid on the full infinite graph. Unlike the earlier confined model, the proof does not require a compact resolvent or a discrete spectrum. This provides a mathematical starting point for investigating separated localized two-state systems in the same network. It does not yet establish multiple independently controllable qubits, state preparation for the plateau Hamiltonian, noise robustness, or experimental feasibility.

The substantive theorem and its supporting results have passed Lean and Mathlib verification. All 13 selected propositions passed independent Comparator verification using the Lean default, NanoDa and con-ron kernels. This sixth result is prepared for Palomar submission, but is not yet registered. Neither independent human peer review nor a novelty or priority assessment is claimed.
entries.title: Exact Double Eigenvalue and Spectral Isolation on an Infinite Ammann–Beenker Graph with a Bounded Plateau Potential

entries.abstract: In the binomial-moment linear program for the largest probability that all k-wise independent Bernoulli bits are 1, every interior exceptional basis transition at bias p has a reflected exceptional transition at bias 1-p. This establishes Conjecture 5.11 of Berend, Ernst, Kontorovich and Kumar over its full stated range of n and even k; it does not address the rationality of breakpoints.
entries.title: Reflection of exceptional breakpoints for k-wise independent bits

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proof that for the simple random walk on ℤ², almost surely the maximal local time Tₙ up to time n satisfies 1/(4π) ≤ liminf Tₙ/(log n)² ≤ limsup Tₙ/(log n)² ≤ 1/π (Erdős and Taylor 1960). The development is elementary: block independence and the fixed-time Markov property, exact return counts by the 45° rotation and Wallis' product, renewal at the first return, last-exit decomposition, Borel–Cantelli along dyadic and geometric times.
entries.title: Erdős–Taylor theorem: the maximal local time of the planar simple random walk is of order (log n)² (Erdős Problem 1166, variant)

entries.abstract: For a finite quantum ensemble with n ≥ 2 labels and optimal discrimination error e, the largest possible conditional subentropy is the subentropy of the prior (1−e, e/(n−1), …, e/(n−1)). Identical pure signals with this prior attain the bound at every admissible error. The inverse curve gives the minimum possible error at each admissible conditional subentropy, even at fixed positive signal dimension.
entries.title: A sharp lower bound on quantum state discrimination error from conditional subentropy

entries.abstract: For every integer r ≥ 3 there is a δ > 0 such that every real number in [1 − δ, 1] is the ordinary Turán density of a family of finite simple r-uniform hypergraphs. The family may be infinite. Its density is the limit of the largest number of edges in an n-vertex hypergraph avoiding the family, divided by the binomial coefficient n choose r. This formalizes Theorem 1.1 of Liu and Pikhurko.
entries.title: Intervals of hypergraph Turán densities

entries.abstract: At twice as many pigeons as holes, the plain pigeonhole principle requires exponentially larger real twin-literal Nullstellensatz coefficient mass than the functional version. The compared theorem is the explicit diagonal separation.
entries.title: A coefficient-mass separation for the pigeonhole principle

entries.abstract: No 93 by 93 zero-one incidence matrix has all row and column sums 10 and pairwise row intersections of size at most one. There is no group action, automorphism or cyclicity hypothesis.
entries.title: Nonexistence of an unrestricted symmetric configuration 93_10

entries.abstract: Four existence theorems on unit fractions, each checked by the Lean kernel from an explicit or implicit witness. (1) An all-odd Giuga sequence: 26 odd integers with Σ1/x − 1/∏x = 1 (Borwein–Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn 1996, Problem 3). (2) Pairwise-coprime integers > 1 with Σ1/x + 1/∏x = 2, for which Brenton–Hill (1988) wrote "no solution is known". (3) A Giuga sequence of value 2 (BBBG Problem 7). (4) Two distinct Giuga sequences with the same product (BBBG Problem 8). Results 2–4 come from one 830-step implicit chain whose elements are too large to write down; it is certified by a residue checker proved sound in Lean. Production: the results, the search programs and this Lean formalization were produced by AI agents (Claude, Anthropic) in a project run by Doug Phillips. He set the goals, directed the work and is responsible for this entry, but he did not independently verify the mathematics. Correctness of the stated theorems rests on the kernel checks recorded here. No human mathematician has yet reviewed the work.
entries.title: An odd Giuga sequence, the Brenton–Hill equation with n₀ = 2, and Borwein et al.'s Giuga Problems 7 and 8

entries.abstract: No strictly increasing natural list beginning at 1 with seven denominations has orderly first three prefixes, nonorderly prefixes of lengths four through six, and an orderly full system.
entries.title: Seven-denomination case of Van Cott–Zhang Conjecture 5.2(1)

entries.abstract: An independent Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem of Liam Kruer and Jensen Kohlmeyer (2026) resolving both parts of Erdős Problem 14. For every A subset N and every N >= 2 * 10000^4, the number of integers in {1, ..., N} not uniquely representable as an unordered sum of two elements of A is at least sqrt(N) / 6000. This establishes Part (i) (nonUniqueSumCount A >> N^(1/2 - eps) for all eps > 0) and refutes the Part (ii) question (no A has nonUniqueSumCount A = o(sqrt(N))). The compared declarations in `Challenge.lean` match `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/14.lean` for Part (i) and state the exact negation of the open existential question for Part (ii).
entries.title: Erdős Problem 14 (Parts (i) and (ii)): Uniform square-root lower bound for non-unique sums

entries.abstract: For finite classical random variables A, B and C, subentropy satisfies Q(AB) + Q(BC) ≥ Q(B) + Q(ABC). Equality holds exactly when A is a function of B almost surely or C is a function of B almost surely. For every t ≥ 0, the pointwise inequality also holds for unnormalized nonnegative tables.
entries.title: Classical strong subadditivity of subentropy

entries.abstract: For every positive integer N, the positive integers representable as a sum of distinct reciprocals of denominators at most N form an initial segment.
entries.title: Erdős Problem #308 at every height

entries.abstract: An independent Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization resolving Sanders' Question 5.1 (Ben Green's Open Problem 51 at density 1/2), following the proof of Jensen Kohlmeyer and Liam Kruer (2026).
