The compared declaration matches `Green51.green_51.one_half` verbatim from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures: for every k > 0, there exists a constant c : Nat such that for all sufficiently large n and every A subset F_2^n of density alpha > 1/2 - k / sqrt(n), the sumset A + A contains an affine coset of dimension at least n - c (codimension at most c). As a proof-level intermediate step inside `Solution.lean` (not stated in the compared theorem's type), the proof constructs a linear subspace of codimension at most ceil(1 + 256 * e * k^2).
entries.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 51 at density one half (Sanders' Question 5.1)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem of Jensen Kohlmeyer and Liam Kruer (2026) resolving the radius-2 question in Ben Green's Open Problem 40: the asymptotic binary linear covering density f(2) equals 1. Using admissible binary quadratic maps and a codimension-doubling interpolation step, we construct linear covering subspaces of radius 2 of arbitrarily large ambient dimension whose covering density approaches 1, matching `Green40.green_40.f_two_eq_one` verbatim from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures.
entries.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 40 (radius 2): asymptotically optimal binary linear covering codes

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib disproof of Farideh Firoozbakht's 2015 conjecture on OEIS A086766 (`OeisA86766.conjecture2` in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures), which asserted that for every positive integer n not of the form 10^m there exists r >= 1 such that the r-fold decimal concatenation of n followed by the digit 1 is prime. We exhibit two explicit 6-digit counterexamples, n = 104040 and n = 750760, proving via algebraic difference-of-squares factorizations that every candidate is composite for all r >= 1.
entries.title: Disproof of Firoozbakht's conjecture on OEIS A086766

entries.abstract: A computer-assisted proof that Dürer's conjecture and the strong and weak flat Dürer conjectures (every convex polyhedron has a net after sufficiently strong squeezing along every, respectively some, axis) are false, by convex polyhedra with triangular faces and no non-overlapping edge unfolding: an explicit rational polyhedron with 276 vertices and 548 triangular faces after every vertical squeeze by a factor at most 2⁻³²⁷⁶⁸; its bottom cap, with 71 vertices and 137 triangular faces, as an arbitrarily flat convex cap with no net; and one explicit polyhedron with 274·2¹⁸⁴ + 2⁹³ + 6 vertices that has no net after a squeeze by any factor 0 < s ≤ 1 along any axis.
entries.title: Counterexamples to Dürer's conjecture and its flat variants

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization for Graham and Harary's hypercube diameter-preserving spanning subgraph problem: proves the universal lower bound 2^n + ceil((2^n - 2n)/(n - 1)) <= f(n) for all n >= 2, raises the asymptotic second-term coefficient to 3/2 on the scale 2^n/(n - 1), and certifies 39 <= f(5) <= 40, f(6) >= 76, f(7) >= 150, f(8) >= 294, and lower bounds for every dimension 17 <= n <= 32. Coverage by this package's Palomar comparison: of the companion paper's 14 main results, 5 are compared in Lean in full (36%; Theorems 1, 3, 9 and 11 and Proposition 13) and 1 in part (Proposition 12: its instances f(6) >= 76 and f(8) >= 294, not its general certificate bridge); 7 more (Corollary 2, Proposition 4, Lemma 5, Theorem 6 and Propositions 7, 8 and 10) are proved in this package's Lean library but not compared; Proposition 14 is outside this comparison (the Lean library rules out valid 19-edge subgraphs of Q_4; its count of 8,320 labelled 20-edge graphs in 30 classes is by external enumeration only); Conjecture 15 is open and not counted. Companion write-up and prior-work search log (including Google Scholar sweep on 2026-11-22) are published at https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/hypercube-edge-bounds; no priority is claimed over unread sources (the full body of Bouabdallah-Delorme-Djelloul 1995 and Djelloul's 1993 thesis could not be accessed).
entries.title: Lower Bounds on Diameter-Preserving Spanning Subgraphs of the Hypercube

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization disproving the Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture as stated in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (`PierceBirkhoff.pierce_birkhoff_conjecture`). Following Lai, Lim, and Ren (arXiv:2609.10420, 2026), we construct a piecewise-quadratic function on R^30 identified with pairs of symmetric 5x5 real matrices, prove that it admits a finite closed semi-algebraic polynomial cover (`IsPiecewiseMvPolynomial`), and prove directly that it cannot be written as a finite supremum of finite infima of multivariate polynomials.
entries.title: Disproof of the Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture in dimension 30

entries.abstract: Complete Lean 4 formalization of the lexicographically sharp all-L^1 Landau-Kolmogorov inequality on any compact interval [a, b] (a < b) and every order n = k + 1 >= 1: ||f^(n)||_1 <= 4^n n! (b-a)^(-n) ||f||_1 + ((b-a)/2) B_n ||f^(n+1)||_1 for f in W^(n+1,1)([a,b]), where B_n = 1 - 2^n/(n+1) + 2^(n+1)/(n+1) sum_{m=1}^{floor((n+1)/2)} (-1)^(m-1) cos^(n+1)(m pi/(n+2)). The development constructs the (n+1)-point moving-node Chebyshev divided- difference operator driven by the eigenvalues of a symmetric tridiagonal Jacobi matrix, proves unconditionally for every n >= 1 that the Peano error profile E_n is strictly decreasing on [0, 1] and attains its unique global maximum on [-1, 1] at t = 0 with value B_n, proves optimality of both constants on C^infty([a,b]), and characterizes equality in C^(n+1)([a,b]) as scalar multiples of the rescaled second-kind Chebyshev polynomial U_n.
entries.title: Sharp Second Constants in L^1 Landau-Kolmogorov Inequalities on a Finite Interval

entries.abstract: For every finite simple graph whose graph and delta complement have no isolated vertices, the sum of their total-domination numbers is at most the number of vertices plus twice the number of distinct vertex degrees of the original graph. This is Conjecture 4 of Pinhe Chen.
entries.title: Chen's total-domination conjecture for the delta complement

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof of the Mirsky–Newman theorem in two forms, both stated word for word as in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (FC) at commit ea8e3e198ded6fc73efb7f5653b74b28ac4ae1a8. The first form (Erdős problem 947) says that no finite family of residue classes with pairwise distinct moduli n_i ≥ 2 partitions the integers, so there is no exact covering system with distinct moduli. The second form (a variant of Erdős problem 1190) says that if residue classes a_n mod n, for n in a finite set S of integers all greater than m ≥ 1, are pairwise disjoint, then the sum of 1/n over S is less than 1. Both are derived from one finite roots-of-unity lemma: pairwise disjoint residue classes with distinct moduli ≥ 2, all dividing N > 0, cannot cover {0, …, N−1}. The lemma is proved by summing ζ^x over {0, …, N−1}, where ζ is a primitive root of unity of order equal to the largest modulus. This entry gives an Apache-2.0-licensed, Comparator-checked proof of both FC statements; at the pinned commit FC links no formal proof of the second.
entries.title: Mirsky–Newman: no exact covering system with distinct moduli (Erdős problems 947 and 1190)

entries.abstract: Self-contained, pure-kernel Lean 4 formalization proving that for every integer n ≥ 3 (both odd and even), no unimodular Alltop phase function exists on 𝔽₂ⁿ and no n-qubit pure state generates 2ⁿ pairwise mutually unbiased orthonormal bases under the n-qubit Pauli (product Weyl–Heisenberg) group. Resolves Conjecture 1 and the unrestricted product-WH MUB question of Damski et al. (arXiv:2603.15550) and rules out the product WH-MUB maximizer mechanism conjectured by Liu, Low, and Yin (Quantum Sci. Technol. 11, 015035, 2026; Open Quantum Problem E28) for n ≥ 4. Also formalizes sharpness at n = 2, the strong odd-n two-valued Pauli-spectrum obstruction, the strict phase-state Gowers U³ bound > 2 - 2⁻ⁿ, and exact closed-form Pauli 4th moments for a GL(n, 𝔽₂)-invariant spike+uniform family recovering the 3-qubit Hoggar SIC (F₃ = 16/9) and certifying a 4-qubit unit state with F₄ < 2.150521. AI-assistance disclosure: the bulk of the technical work (proof discovery, Lean 4 formalization, companion scripts, and manuscript drafting) was carried out using AI systems under the author's problem selection, direction, and oversight; mathematical validity of all compared theorems rests on Lean 4's kernel verification.
entries.title: Non-Existence of Multi-Qubit Pauli-Covariant MUB Fiducial States and Alltop Phase Functions on F_2^n (n >= 3)

entries.abstract: This Lean and Mathlib development proves Graffiti.pc Conjecture 261. For a finite simple connected graph G of order at least two, let S be its degree-two vertices and let L(G) be the maximum number of leaves over its spanning trees. The total domination number of G is at least 2|N_G(S) \ S| / L(G), where N_G(S) consists of the vertices adjacent to some vertex of S. The formal proof combines a count of edges incident to S with a leaf bound from a spanning tree preserving a total dominating set. The compared theorem states the inequality with rational division.
entries.title: A proof of Written on the Wall II Conjecture 261

entries.abstract: For an integrable floored scalar observation model, the package proves a lower masking rate, an actual separating read, a finite-layer estimate under the continuum error envelope, a calibrated three-read certificate, and local finite-menu masking at a nonaligned reference.
entries.title: Quantitative and calibrated finite-read statements for null-clock scans

entries.abstract: Pure-kernel Lean 4 formalization resolving the two-qubit (n = 2) maximal magic conjecture of Liu, Low, and Yin (Quantum Sci. Technol. 11, 015035, 2026; Open Quantum Problem E28) for all Stabilizer Rényi Entropy (SRE) orders α ≥ 2. Using the SU(4) ≅ Spin(6) reduction onto the positively oriented skew-orthogonal manifold in SO(6) and an exact degree-8 B₆⁺-equivariant rational sum-of-squares certificate verified by definitional equality inside Lean's kernel, the formalization proves the sharp upper bound M_α(|ψ⟩) ≤ (1/(1-α)) log((1 + 3·4^(1-α))/4) (in particular max M_2 = log(16/7)), proves attainment by |ψ_MUB⟩ = (1/2)(1, 1, 1, i), classifies all maximizers as a single two-qubit Clifford orbit of exact cardinality 480 coinciding with the two-qubit Pauli 5-MUB fiducial states, and proves the exact Wootters concurrence dichotomy C ∈ {1/2, 1/√2} with 192 / 288 state counts. AI-assistance disclosure: the bulk of the technical work (proof discovery, SOS certificate pipeline, Lean 4 formalization, and manuscript drafting) was carried out using AI systems under the author's problem selection, direction, and oversight; mathematical correctness rests on Lean 4's kernel verification and the standalone exact-integer Python certificate verifier.
entries.title: Rigorous Resolution of the Two-Qubit Maximal Magic Conjecture

entries.abstract: Erdős Problem 707 asks whether every finite Sidon set of natural numbers is contained in a perfect difference set. Every Sidon set of size 3 extends (Sawin). For size 4, Mueller (MathOverflow answer 502053) found {0,1,3,11} and {0,1,4,11} and showed that neither lies in any Singer (Desarguesian) difference set, but whether they extend to a non-Desarguesian cyclic plane is open. This formalization proves, in Lean 4 with Mathlib and only the standard axioms, two restrictions that need no assumption on the plane: (1) neither set lies in a perfect difference set of even order (any modulus n), by Baer's argument that 2 is then a multiplier; (2) {0,1,3,11} lies in no finite perfect difference set whose order is divisible by 2 or by 3, by Hall's multiplier theorem, which is proved here from scratch for planar difference sets (Frobenius in the group algebra (ZMod p)[ZMod n]) with no prime-power assumption. The question for orders with all prime factors at least 5 (for {0,1,3,11}) and for odd orders (for {0,1,4,11}) is not settled.
entries.title: Mueller's four-element candidate counterexamples to Erdős Problem 707 in cyclic planes of order divisible by 2 or 3

entries.abstract: Every non-Hadamard real sign matrix has a direction of strictly negative curvature when its entries are allowed to vary through complex phases. We prove an energy-only criterion for unique one-entry repair and construct infinitely many matrices trapped under every one-entry and two-entry sign change. Further results classify rank-two Gram defects and provide constructive phase escape and exact rounding certificates. We also characterize four-phase accessibility under row and column phases, prove a signed complex-structure criterion for the corresponding real Hadamard construction from quaternary matrices, and give quantitative Fourier-Dita obstructions showing when these phase-based families cannot reach fourth-root entries. See README.md for the main theorem statements, RESULTS.md for further results, paper/main.pdf for proofs and citations, and TECHNICAL.md for formalization coverage and build details.
entries.title: Gram defects, phase escape, and exact rounding

entries.abstract: We characterize normalized real and complex Hadamard matrices through the local extremum behavior of every tensor power of entrywise power energies. We construct almost flat real orthogonal matrices in every sufficiently large dimension with a quantitative rate, and give infinite families of strict local minima that do not attain the global minimum of quartic energy. We also obtain quantitative existence bounds for sign matrices with condition numbers approaching one, and a subpolynomial bound on the logarithmic deficit from Hadamard's maximal-determinant bound. See README.md for the main theorem statements, RESULTS.md for further results, paper/main.pdf for proofs and citations, and TECHNICAL.md for formalization coverage and build details.
entries.title: Tensor stability and flat orthogonal optimization

entries.abstract: Let x_n = tan(arctan 1 + arctan 2 + ⋯ + arctan n) = B_n / A_n, where (1 + i)(1 + 2i)⋯(1 + ni) = A_n + B_n i in the Gaussian integers. Amdeberhan, Medina and Moll (2008) conjectured that x_n is never an integer for n ≥ 5. Ono (arXiv:2607.05739, Corollary 1.2) proved that there is an n₀ such that x_n is not an integer for every n ≥ n₀ outside a sparse exceptional set E = {n ≥ 5 : |x_n| > n/2 + 1}, without giving a value of n₀. This formalization proves, in Lean 4 with Mathlib and only the standard axioms, that n₀ = 5 works: for every n ≥ 5 with n ∉ E, A_n does not divide B_n. The proof combines a reduction (two distinct primes p > 2n dividing 1 + k² for some k ≤ n force |x_n| ≥ 2n + 2 at an integer value), twelve kernel-checked prime certificates covering 5 ≤ n ≤ 499,950,001,250, and a fully formal Chebyshev-type argument for all larger n. It does not prove the Amdeberhan–Medina–Moll conjecture: the indices in E are not treated, and E is not known to be finite.
entries.title: An explicit form (n₀ = 5) of Ono's theorem on integer values of tan(arctan 1 + ⋯ + arctan n)

entries.abstract: In 1979, Paul Erdős conjectured that powers of 2 avoid the ternary digit 2 only for n ∈ {0, 2, 8}. In the dual negative-power direction, we formalize the complete classification of ternary digit distributions for reciprocals 1/2^n: for all n ≥ 4, the base-3 expansion of 1/2^n contains the digit 2. The proof establishes the Gap Lemma for the coset {1, 3} mod 8 (maximum gap bounded by 6) and uses the Lifting-the-Exponent Lemma (LTE) to prove that the cyclic subgroup ⟨3⟩ mod 2^n surjects onto the entire coset {1, 3} mod 8, forcing the cyclic orbit to intersect the digit-2 target interval.
entries.title: The Negative-Power Erdős Ternary Digit Theorem

entries.abstract: For a sequence of points on the circle, let M_n and m_n be the longest and shortest arcs between consecutive points among the first n points. De Bruijn and Erdős proved that the best possible values of limsup n·M_n, liminf n·m_n and limsup M_n/m_n are 1/log 2, 1/log 4 and 2. This formalizes all three equalities as stated in formal-conjectures (Erdős Problem 1221, variant r_one).
entries.title: Erdős Problem 1221: the case r = 1

entries.abstract: How many real numbers λ₁(x), …, λₙ(x) must be computed to recover a vector x of a d-dimensional real normed space to within ε, when every λᵢ is continuous in x and may be chosen after the previous values have been seen? The answer is exponentially smaller than for linear or for non-adaptive continuous measurements: ⌈log₂ d⌉ + 1 measurements suffice for every accuracy (Krieg, Novak and Ullrich), and ⌈log₂(d+1)⌉ are necessary (Ullrich). The lower bound is a Borsuk–Ulam theorem for adaptive schemes: if 2^n ≤ d, then on every sphere some antipodal pair x, -x produces the same n values, although the information map is in general discontinuous.
entries.title: A Borsuk–Ulam theorem for adaptive continuous measurements

entries.abstract: 两题最小反例分别恰有 11 和 14 个顶点。完整证明更小的有限连通简单图满足原不等式。
entries.title: WOWII 第 255、256 题的最小反例

entries.abstract: The permutohedron in R^n is the convex hull of the rearrangements of (n, n-1, ..., 1). This entry proves that for every ordered partition of the coordinates into m nonempty blocks the corresponding face is an exposed face of dimension n - m, and conversely that every nonempty exposed face is the face of an ordered partition, with k blocks when its dimension is n - k. For the ridges (m = 3, blocks of sizes a, b, c) it proves that the plane through the centre and the ridge is {y : sum y = 0, c(a+b) sum over B1 + a(b+c) sum over B3 = 0}; that two ridges give the same plane exactly when they are equal or reverses, or both have a = c and the same or complementary middle blocks; and that the number of distinct planes is the closed formula of OEIS A402191 for every n >= 3 (values 3, 15, 65, 225, 770, 2443 for n = 3 to 8); for n >= 3 the count is also proved for the set of planes through the centre and the nonempty exposed faces of dimension n - 3, defined without partitions. For the planes through the centre parallel to the facets (the resonance arrangement), it proves that two facets share a plane exactly when their sets are equal or complementary, that there are 2^(n-1) - 1 such planes, that each facet is nonempty and its plane has dimension n - 2, and exactly which of them are also ridge planes: all of them for odd n, all but 2^(n-2) for even n. The source paper (DICTO, The Vacuus and the Resonus) calls the two families the Vacuus and the Resonus. The proofs build on TauCeti's formalization of Rado's theorem. Audience: readers of polytope geometry and Mathlib users working with convex sets and permutations.
entries.title: Planes Through the Centre of the Permutohedron: Faces, Vacuus Plates and Their Count, in Lean

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of the balanced reserve and matching results in Lemmas 4.11–4.14 of Chen and Shan’s An Asymptotically Sharp Form of the Overfull Conjecture. Signed edge weights realize prescribed margins in dense bipartite graphs. These weights yield sampling probabilities with balanced expected degrees in cyclic directed pairs. Short path deletions restore exact balance in a dense tripartite graph, and a matching theorem packs edge-disjoint perfect matchings across overlapping bipartite graphs.
entries.title: Chen–Shan balanced reserves and disjoint matching packings

entries.abstract: An orthonormal terminal frame with k exceptional Schmidt amplitudes has a replacement on 2k coordinates preserving all positive exceptional spectra and all pairs of power-residual exponents simultaneously. With at least k background copies the unnormalized score set stabilizes. For two exceptional amplitudes this gives the attained fixed-state two-step Hardy maximum and an explicit loss below the plastic ceiling for every extra background copy.
entries.title: The Exact Two-Step Hardy Ladder Optimum for Repeated Schmidt Levels

entries.abstract: A formalization of a proof of Swanepoel's Conjecture on Penny Graphs. The conjecture asks for the maximum number of edges in a triangle-free penny graph on n vertices. Let this quantity be denoted as f(n). Previous results have shown that f(n) >= floor(2n - 2 square root n). Prior work proved the approximate upper bound f(n) <= floor(2n - 1.65 square root of n). This work formalizes a proof that the upper bound is the conjectured floor(2n - 2 square root of n). This result proves the stated conjecture unconditionally and affirmatively.
entries.title: Swanepoel's Conjecture Full Proof

entries.abstract: 两题不等式中最大的普适实系数均为 1。第 256 题的系数在连通二分图类中也最优。
entries.title: WOWII 第 255、256 题的最优系数

entries.abstract: The Albert algebra J = H3(O) is the 27-dimensional real Jordan algebra of 3x3 Hermitian octonionic matrices. An atom is an idempotent of trace one (a pure state). Its ideal yes-no test updates a state by the Lueders rule, and a word of outcomes has as probability the trace of the updated, unnormalised state. If finitely many atoms generate J, from any state no sequential projective representation on a real, complex or quaternionic Hilbert space reproduces all their word probabilities, and a finite linear inequality valid in every such representation fails by a positive margin from every state. Not generating J is equivalent to lying in a special unital subalgebra, and to one family of projections on C^6 or C^24 serving every state. For four generating atoms, from the maximally mixed state a representation on C^12 reproduces every word of length at most six, but none every word of length at most seven. A polynomial A in thirteen traces is nonnegative for four atoms and positive exactly when they generate J; its maximum is 4/19683, and when A = 0 every state has a representation on C^6. Three atoms never generate J, and every state has a representation on C^3. The atoms are exactly the primitive idempotents.
entries.title: On sequential ideal measurements in the exceptional Jordan algebra

entries.abstract: For n at least three, a finite simple undirected graph on 3n vertices has real adjacency rank at most five if the sum of squared differences between its decreasing ordered adjacency eigenvalues and (2n, 0, ..., 0, -n, -n) is strictly less than 2/3. This answers Jovanović, Sedlar and Škrekovski's Problem 21 without a connectedness requirement. The proof reduces to nonsingular principal submatrices of orders six or seven and uses exact Lean-checked finite certificates.
entries.title: Ordered spectral proximity forces adjacency rank at most five

entries.abstract:
Can we prepare a chosen quantum state using very weak controls while keeping the two energy levels of its supporting space separated from the rest of an infinite network? For the particular confined Ammann–Beenker graph studied here, the answer is yes.

The first registered result, [PALOMAR-2026-11-06-000012 (version 1)](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-11-06-000012&version=1), establishes exactly two independent localized states at a common energy. A separate Lean theorem certifies a gap of 1/128 from all other real spectral energies at that setting. [PALOMAR-2026-11-23-000017 (version 1)](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-11-23-000017&version=1) shows how changing a single edge splits their energy. [PALOMAR-2026-11-25-000001 (version 1)](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-11-25-000001&version=1) establishes exact preparation without leakage using two coordinated controls, and [PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000015 (version 1)](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-11-26-000015&version=1) establishes spectral protection for sufficiently weak ideal controls. The new theorem brings exact preparation and spectral protection together.

The dark and bright states are the normalized sum and difference of the two original localized patterns. Starting from the dark state, choose any normalized complex superposition of these states, including either state alone. Also choose any positive control-strength limit ε and any fraction f strictly between zero and one of the certified gap to retain (for example, 99%). The theorem constructs three consecutive pulses of the same finite duration that reach the chosen state exactly up to a common phase of modulus one, which does not change the physical ray.

In each of the first and third pulses, all eight inter-ring edges are changed by a common signed amount, which may differ between the two pulses. The middle pulse changes a common onsite parameter at eight first-ring vertices. By making the pulses longer and reducing their strengths in inverse proportion, we preserve the desired rotation while making the combined control size |δ| + 2|η| at most ε, where δ is the onsite change and η the edge-strength change.

Throughout the protocol the state remains normalized, with exactly zero leakage outside the original two-state space, including at both switching times. In each of the three control settings, each of the two localized energy levels is separated from every real spectral energy outside those levels by at least f/128. Every eigenvector at either level is confined to the original space, and there are no other real spectral energies between them. The two levels may coincide when both controls vanish. The theorem gives an explicit duration and common phase.

This is an exact result for the unbounded Hamiltonian on the full infinite graph, not a two-state approximation or a finite simulation. The constructed state is continuous, its real and imaginary parts lie in the natural operator domain, and it satisfies the full Schrödinger equations on each open pulse interval. Differentiability at the switches is not asserted. The result does not claim a general full-space quantum propagator, arbitrary-target preparation at zero control strength, retention of the entire certified gap, robustness to noise or imperfect coordination, optimal pulse durations, or experimental feasibility.

The substantive proof and all 19 selected candidate propositions passed full Lean verification and independent statement comparison using the Lean default, NanoDa and con-ron kernels. Separate Palomar registry verification and registration have not yet been completed. Independent human peer review and assessment of novelty are not claimed.
entries.title: Exact Leakage-Free Quantum State Preparation with Arbitrarily Weak Controls and Prescribed Spectral Protection on an Infinite Ammann–Beenker Graph

entries.abstract: Each player independently keeps a share of one secret qubit with probability p. A false approval occurs when Ganguly's circuit rule approves the surviving group and it cannot recover the qubit. Among finite connected simple graphs with one designated dealer and a nonempty, pairwise-intersecting family of approved groups, the supremum of this probability is zero at p = 0 and p = 1, equals p for 0 < p ≤ 1/2, and equals one for 1/2 < p < 1.
entries.title: Sharp false-approval probability in graph-state quantum secret sharing

entries.abstract: For every n at least eleven there is an n-denomination coin system in which greedy change is optimal for every amount in the first three prefixes and the full system, but not in any intervening prefix. This refutes the general prohibition in Conjecture 5.2(1) at each length 3r+1 for r at least four. At every length 3r+2 for r at least four there is a counterexample to the exhaustiveness claim in 5.2(3), outside both families D and G.
entries.title: Van Cott–Zhang prefix patterns for every length at least eleven

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization and algebraic adaptation of the equivalence between the planar Jacobian conjecture and the four-variable Hessian conjecture. Over every algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the two polynomial-inverse conjectures are equivalent. Over arbitrary characteristic-zero fields, the corresponding same-field injectivity statements are equivalent with determinant-one normalization on the Hessian side. Neither conjecture is proved unconditionally.
entries.title: Equivalence of the Four-Variable Hessian and Planar Jacobian Conjectures

entries.abstract: A connected non-bipartite graph on 24 vertices has radius 10 and floods in three synchronous rounds from four sources, so its optimal four-source flooding time t satisfies 4t ≤ 12 < 13. Repeating the gadget gives a counterexample to Turau's Section 8 inequality for every source count k ≥ 4, with exact radius floor(5k/2) and optimal k-source flooding time at most 3.
entries.title: A counterexample and infinite family for Turau's amnesiac flooding conjecture

entries.abstract: For a field K, the tensor rank R_K(<n,l,m>) is the least number r of products in a bilinear algorithm A*B = sum_{k<r} alpha_k(A) beta_k(B) C_k for the product of an n x l and an l x m matrix over K (alpha_k, beta_k linear forms, C_k fixed matrices). This entry proves in Lean 4 with Mathlib that R_K(<4,2,4>) = 26 for every field K, with no assumption on the characteristic, finiteness or algebraic closedness of K. The upper bound 26 is the value for p = n = 4 of the formula ceil((3pn + max(n,p))/2) of Hopcroft and Kerr (Cornell Technical Report 69-44, 1969, Theorem 1; SIAM J. Appl. Math. 20 (1971)); here it is proved by an explicit algorithm with 26 products and integer coefficients in {-1, 0, 1}, found by the project's own search and checked by the Lean kernel. In that report Hopcroft and Kerr conjectured (pp. 27-28) that their algorithm is optimal for all p and n, which for <4,2,4> means 26 multiplications; they proved lower bounds only for 2 x 2 times 2 x n and 3 x 2 times 2 x 3, for programs with integer constants and without commutativity, by reduction modulo 2. To our knowledge, a proof of the lower bound 26 is new (literature search recorded in lit/ of this repository); the previously known proved lower bound was 25 (J. Yang, arXiv:2609.14393, Theorem 2, which the development also formalises). The proof of the lower bound builds on Yang's normal form (N1), (N2) for <n,2,m> and extends it with new steps. Lengths below 25 are excluded by Yang's Theorem 2. A decomposition of length 25 is put into a generic normal form over the field of rational functions K(S, T) and read over its algebraic closure. There, Theorem A leaves four rank cases (3,6), (4,7), (5,7), (5,8); Theorem B excludes (4,7) and (5,7) and shows that (3,6) is symmetric; Theorem C shows that the generic normal form is not symmetric. The case (5,8) splits into two sub-cases: sub-case A is excluded by Theorem E, and in sub-case B Theorem F, with Lemma Z and the transposed decomposition, forces a symmetry, which Theorem C excludes. The work was carried out by AI models directed by the repository owner; no human mathematician has reviewed the proof.
entries.title: The tensor rank of 4x2x4 matrix multiplication is 26 over every field

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 formalization of the classical characterizations of Wolstenholme primes: for a prime p > 7, C(2p−1, p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p⁴) holds if and only if p³ divides the numerator of the harmonic number H_{p−1}, and if and only if p divides the numerator of the Bernoulli number B_{p−3}. It also proves Wolstenholme's theorem C(2p−1, p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p³) for primes p > 3, and Glaisher's congruence 3·H_{p−1,2} ≡ 2p·B_{p−3} (mod p²). The statements of the first three results are copied verbatim from Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures. The proof of the Bernoulli characterization avoids Kummer's congruences: it combines Faulhaber's formula and von Staudt–Clausen with a doubling argument k ↦ 2k mod p.
entries.title: Wolstenholme primes: harmonic and Bernoulli characterizations

entries.abstract: Unconditional pure core Lean 4 formalization (zero external dependencies, zero Mathlib imports, zero sorry, zero native_decide, standard axioms only) determining the exact last exception c*(k) for the 2-colour Rado number R(c, k) of x + y + c = kz for every integer k >= 3, where c*(k) = k(k^2 + k - 4)/2 for odd k and k(k^2 - 2)/2 for even k. Both halves are formalized unconditionally: (1) the companion paper's reflection proof (x |-> N+1-x) of the upper half R(c, k) = LB(c, k) for every valid c > c*(k) (valid means k odd or c even) combined with the general lower bound LB(c, k) of Martinelli and Schaal (2007, Lemma 2), and (2) an explicit boundary colouring showing non-forcing at LB(c*(k), k), i.e., there exists a 2-colouring of [1, LB(c*(k), k)] with no monochromatic solution of x + y + c*(k) = k z (so ¬ Forced (c*(k)) k (LB (c*(k)) k) and c*(k) is an exception to R(c, k) = LB(c, k); finite existence of R(c*(k), k) itself is not formalized). In nu_iff, the property "R(c, k) = LB(c, k) for all valid c >= v" holds iff c*(k) < v, so the least integer cutoff is c*(k) + 1 while the least valid cutoff nu(k) (requiring Valid nu(k) k, i.e., even when k is even) is c*(k) + 1 for odd k and c*(k) + 2 for even k, giving least valid cutoffs 13, 30, 66, 104, 183, 250, 388, 492 for k = 3..10 and settling the Kim-Song-Hwang (2023) conjecture nu(5) = 66. Coverage by this package's Palomar comparison: of the companion paper's 6 main results, 3 are compared in Lean in full (50%; Theorem 1 and Corollaries 2 and 3); Theorems 4 and 5 and Lemma 6 are proved in this package's Lean library but not compared. Abstract claims: 3 of 6 compared in Lean (50%).
entries.title: The Last Exception for Two-Colour Rado Numbers of x + y + c = kz

entries.abstract: Let f(n) be the maximal number of edges of a graph on n vertices in which every cycle has more vertices than chords. Erdős Problem 642 (Hamburger and Szegedy) asks whether f(n) = O(n); this is open. This project proves the bound f(n) = O(n^(3/2)) attributed to Chen, Erdős and Staton, in the explicit form f(n) <= 2 (floor(sqrt n) + 1) n, by a longest path argument.
entries.title: The Chen-Erdős-Staton bound for Erdős Problem 642

entries.abstract: For any matroid on a finite ambient type of rank at most four, the inverse Z-polynomial has positive coefficients through rank and is log-concave. The proof uses a rank-four deletion inequality on flat incidences.
entries.title: Inverse Z-polynomial log-concavity through rank four

entries.abstract: A Mathlib-only Lean formalization of Liu and Meng's separation argument. There exists an infinite binary sequence on which every total computable adaptive betting strategy with uniformly computable-real, nonnegative, fair capital has bounded capital, while the sequence fails a Martin-Löf test for the fair-coin measure. Each strategy queries distinct positions along every possible answer history. Martin-Löf randomness also implies randomness for this strategy convention, so the inclusion is proper. The actual simultaneous affine-block construction, short reconstruction programs, and probability estimates are proved without construction premises.
entries.title: Kolmogorov–Loveland and Martin-Löf randomness

entries.abstract:
An original result on Morrey's problem for integrands on real 2x2 matrices, proved in Lean 4: for every p > 0, an F that is isotropic (invariant under rotations on both sides), positively p-homogeneous and rank-one convex is quasiconvex (Theorem A). The proof for integrands that change sign integrates scaled truncated determinants over the radius (Proposition 6.8: for every convex N with N(0) <= 0, an explicit radial function of N is quasiconvex). What a sign condition adds, range by range:

For p >= 2 and F >= 0, F is polyconvex, hence quasiconvex, with a polyaffine support at every matrix in closed form (Theorems 1.1 and 1.2); this answers Question 1.7 of Guerra and Kristensen (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 245, 2022), who proved it at the multiples of orthogonal matrices. For p > 2, F is polyconvex if and only if it is rank-one convex and nonnegative, and for p = 2 no sign condition is needed (Theorem 1.3). For 1 <= p < 2 and F >= 0, F has at every matrix a touching minorant that is a nonnegative combination of the Burkholder function and its mirror image (Theorem 1.5). Hence, for 1 < p < 2, F is quasiconvex (Corollary 1.6 (a)), by the quasiconvexity of the Burkholder function, which Proposition 6.8 gives for every p > 1 (Corollary 6.11). Proposition 6.8 rests on the quasiconvexity of the truncated determinant, claimed as Theorem 1 of the preprint of Agazzi et al., arXiv:2609.28311, and taken here from lean4-iwaniec, the Lean formalization with which that preprint was audited. For p = 1, F is convex, with no sign condition, a theorem of Dacorogna (Corollary 1.6 (b)). For 0 < p < 1, F is zero, with neither isotropy nor a sign condition (Proposition 1.7).

The paper is docs/HomogeneousIsotropic/paper/main.tex in the repository.
entries.title: Morrey's problem for homogeneous isotropic integrands on 2x2 matrices, in Lean

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization (208 audited declarations, zero sorry, zero native_decide, standard axioms only) covering three families of exact girth theorems for the Lazebnik-Ustimenko algebraically defined bipartite graphs D(k, F), formalizing results of the companion paper, among them a second proof of an earlier binary theorem: (1) Theorem 5(b) of the companion paper: exact girth D(9, F) = girth D(10, F) = 14 for every finite field F with |F| >= 4 in both the working (DS28 Section 6.1) and original minus-sign representations, closing characteristics 2 and 3 (q = 2^m >= 4 and q = 3^m >= 9, left open by Pikuta 2008), closing the empty DS28 Table 7 cells (9, 27), (10, 27), (9, 32), (10, 32), and proving at least two admissible cycle parameters exist whenever |F| >= 4; (2) Independent Lean 4 proof of the earlier complete binary girth law of Cheng, Chen, and Tang (2014) (quoted in Xu, Cheng, and Tang 2023, Example 1): girth D(k, 2) = 2^s for every s >= 3 and every k >= 2 with 2^(s-1) - 4 < k <= 2^s - 4 in both sign models, proved independently via an affine unipotent 4-step operator T4(p) = (I + N)p + b over ZMod 2, and applied (D2_girth_gt_16_of_ge_13) to prove girth D(k, 2) >= 32 with no 16-cycle for every k >= 13, refuting the conflicting printed claim D(k, 2) ~= 2^(k-3) C_16 (k >= 5) in Lazebnik-Sun-Wang (2017) and Lazebnik-Wang DS28 (2026); and (3) Kernel-verified exact ternary girths D(k, 3) (Theorem 11(a) of the companion paper) including k = 15, 16 (girth 20), k = 47, 48 (52), k = 55, 56 (60), k = 79, 80 (84), k = 99 (104), and k = 103, 104 (108), together with the unconditional tightening 56 <= girth D(52, 3) <= 60. Companion manuscript and verification archive: https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/lazebnik-ustimenko. Coverage by this package's Palomar comparison, against the 5 main results the companion paper counts: 1 is compared in Lean in full (20%; the binary girth law, Proposition 13) and 2 in part (Theorem 5(b), girth 14 in dimensions 9 and 10, for every finite field with at least 4 elements but not for infinite fields; Theorem 11(a), 11 of the 27 exact ternary girths, plus 56 <= girth D(52, 3) <= 60); the universal lower bound (Theorem 5(a)) and the other 16 ternary girths are proved in this package's Lean library but not compared; the ternary table through k = 50 (Theorem 11(b)) combines Lean upper bounds with external search lower bounds and is not compared. Theorems 7 and 9 and Proposition 10 of the paper, outside its count of five, are not proved in this package (it has only Theorem 9's inputs from Theorem 5(b) and Proposition 13); Theorem 5(c), also outside the count, is in the library only as bridges that take the cited lifting theorems as hypotheses.
entries.title: Exact Girths of Lazebnik-Ustimenko Graphs D(k, q): Girth 14 for All |F| >= 4, Independent Proof of the Binary Girth Law, and Ternary Girths

entries.abstract: Two existence theorems on unit fractions, each checked by the Lean kernel from an explicit or implicit witness. (1) The coprime variant of Erdős Problem #307 with 1 excluded: finite sets P, Q of integers greater than 1, each pairwise coprime, with (Σ_{p∈P} 1/p)(Σ_{q∈Q} 1/q) = 1. The statement is formal-conjectures' erdos_307.variants.coprime_one_notMem, listed there and on erdosproblems.com as having no known examples. The witness has 973 elements, most too large to write down. It is encoded by 914 small "deviations" and certified by a residue checker whose soundness is proved in Lean. (2) An all-odd solution of Znám's problem: 24 odd integers greater than 1, each a proper divisor of the product of the others plus 1. No all-odd solution was known (Brenton and Joo, 1995). Production: the results, the search programs and this Lean formalization were produced by AI agents (Claude, Anthropic) in a project run by Doug Phillips. He set the goals, directed the work and is responsible for this entry, but he did not independently verify the mathematics. Correctness of the stated theorems rests on the kernel checks recorded here. No human mathematician has yet reviewed the work.
entries.title: An odd solution of Znám's problem and a solution of the coprime variant of Erdős Problem #307

entries.abstract: For connected symmetric nonnegatively weighted graphs with known positive decay and a cyclic signed port, local responses to continuous time inputs exist and have two derivatives at zero. In the separated-port spectral-band and contraction regime of Theorem A, equality of the first and half-mixed second terminal derivatives in all smooth compactly supported directions on one fixed positive horizon determines the source graph Laplacian and signed port up to the same vertex permutation. The admissible competitor can have any finite size. The spectral-band and contraction conditions apply to the source.
entries.title: Exact single-port graph identification from two response derivatives

entries.abstract: We construct a counterexample to the generalized Nandakumar--Ramana Rao problem: in every dimension d > 17, there are d − 1 continuous functionals on convex bodies and a probability measure such that there is no convex partition of the unit ball into six parts of equal measure on which all these functionals are equalized. We also show that the topological Tverberg conjecture fails for sixfold intersections already in ℝ⁶: we construct a continuous map Δ³⁵ → ℝ⁶ whose images of six pairwise disjoint faces never meet.
entries.title: Sixfold Tverberg Counterexamples and Convex Equipartition Obstructions

entries.abstract: The central contribution is a Lean 4 / Mathlib proof that Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` implies two classical statements: for every delta > 0, |psi(x) - x| <= C x^(1/2 + delta) for all large x (`Submission.chebyshev_psi_error_of_RH`, psi being Mathlib's `Chebyshev.psi`), and for every epsilon > 0 and all large x a prime in (x, x + x^(1/2 + epsilon)] (`Submission.exists_prime_in_short_interval_of_RH`). Both are known under RH: the first is the theorem of section 7 of H. von Koch (1901), who also proves the sharper sqrt(x) log^2 x, and the second follows from it; this work does not claim them as new mathematics. Their proof is a contour shift of the smoothed Chebyshev function of PrimeNumberTheoremAnd (whose files are ported to an earlier Mathlib with mechanical changes, `PNTPort/`) to the line Re s = 1/2 + delta, with two new estimates: zeta'/zeta << log|t| to the right of 1/2 under RH (Borel-Caratheodory on a holomorphic logarithm of zeta), and an interpolated bound on the Mellin transform of the smoothing that keeps the exponent 1/2 (the bound used in PrimeNumberTheoremAnd alone would give 3/4). PrimeNumberTheoremAnd records RH-conditional prime-in-interval statements of this kind as targets with `sorry`. Zero sorries; the advertised theorems depend only on the three standard Lean axioms.
entries.title: RHShortIntervals: psi(x) = x + O(x^(1/2+delta)) and primes in short intervals from the Riemann Hypothesis

entries.abstract: Naik and Selman's Hypothesis B states that every polynomial-time function on binary strings computable with one nonadaptive batch of NP queries can also be computed with logarithmically many adaptive NP queries. We prove that this inclusion implies P = NP, answering their question about its consequence. Conversely, P = NP implies that the two function classes coincide. The proof uses affine hulls of verifier witnesses over the binary field to turn a polynomial-size list of candidate hulls into a deterministic witness search. Lean verifies both directions for total functions in an explicit binary register-machine model.
entries.title: Functional NP Query Compression Is Equivalent to P = NP

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the paper 'Powers of a Prime in the Image of Summatory Valuation Functions', on the question of Nicolas about the powers of 2 in the image of c(n) = sum_{k=1}^{n} 2^{v_2(k)}. It proves the recurrences and the binary formula for c, the equivalence of Theorem thm:equiv, the greedy lemma, the leading term and the recursion on states with its algorithm, the explicit members and non-members, the one-step classification, the families of Nicolas and their counting, the lower bounds for the counting functions A(x) and B(x) (Theorems thm:counting and thm:counting2), the forest of successful states, the bottom-up recursion and the symmetry, the further families of Theorem thm:symfamilies, and the analogue for an arbitrary prime p (Lemma lem:cp, Proposition prop:Fp, Theorems thm:primes, thm:primestep, thm:primefamilies, thm:immediate, thm:primebottomup and Proposition prop:primezero). Everything is proved from Mathlib. The worked numerical examples of the text and the computations of Section sec:experiments are not formalized.
entries.title: SequenceNicolas: powers of a prime in the image of summatory valuation functions

entries.abstract: Let P be a finite polyhedral space with compatible simplex charts of constant curvature κ ∈ {−1,0,1}, let d be the chart dimension, and let n ≥ d. Every short map from P to the corresponding n-dimensional model should admit a uniformly close PL-isometry. In the spherical case the Challenge additionally assumes uniform strict shortness or that the image lies in an open hemisphere.
entries.title: Akopyan's PL Nash–Kuiper–Gromov theorem

entries.abstract: Let r(P_s,t) denote the Ramsey number of the 3-uniform tight path with s edges versus a clique on t vertices. Results of Phelps and Rodl give r(P_2,t)=Theta(t^2/log t). In 2013, Cooper and Mubayi proved that r(P_s,t)=Theta(t^2) for every fixed s at least 4. For the remaining case s=3, they asked for the order of r(P_3,t), a question later reiterated by Bohman, Mubayi and Picollelli. Together, these results give a lower bound of Omega(t^2/log t) and an upper bound of O(t^2) for r(P_3,t). We improve the upper bound to O(t^2/log log t), making progress towards a conjecture of Mattheus, Mubayi, Nie and Verstraete. The main upper bound is formalized unconditionally in Lean 4.
entries.title: On the Ramsey number of a tight path of length 3 versus a clique

entries.abstract: For OEIS A212334, given for n >= 1 by a(n) = sum over 0 <= k < n of C(n,k) C(n-1,k) C(n+k-1,k)^2, with a(0) = 1, a Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that a(p) is congruent to 1 modulo p^5 for every prime p >= 5. Peter Bala recorded this congruence as an observation in the OEIS entry in December 2021. An earlier informal proof of the same congruence is public, and no priority is claimed. The binomial sum is taken as the definition; its agreement with the word-counting definition in OEIS, and the higher prime-power congruences conjectured in the same entry, are not formalized.
entries.title: A supercongruence modulo p^5 for OEIS A212334 (observed by Peter Bala)

entries.abstract: No symmetric incidence configuration exists with 59 points and 59 lines, eight incidences at every point and line, and at most one common line for any two distinct points. The compared declaration states the equivalent binary integer incidence-matrix theorem. It places no restriction on the automorphism group or the cycle types of the leave graphs. The proof derives leave-graph constraints from an arbitrary incidence matrix and closes the resulting finite cases in Lean. Davydov, Faina, Giulietti, Marcugini and Pambianco distinguish this unrestricted case, listed as undecided in their Table 7.1, from the cyclic case in Table 6.1.
entries.title: There is no symmetric configuration 59₈

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization proving that no odd perfect number N = pi^alpha * q_1^(r-1) * ... * q_t^(r-1) has every non-special prime raised to the same exponent r - 1 for any odd prime 3 <= r <= 73 (all 20 odd primes, 1 <= beta <= 36 where r = 2*beta + 1), together with Theorem 1 of the companion paper (notSpecial_of_prime, implied by Kanold's 1941 congruence) that r cannot be the special prime for any odd prime r >= 3. Formalizes the companion paper's proof (Theorem 2, cases r <= 73), which gives second proofs of the 9 prime cases in this range excluded in earlier work and treats the 11 other prime cases through r = 73 (including beta = 9, 15, 20, 21, 23, attempted without success by Cohen and Williams 1985, plus r = 53, 59, 61, 67, 71, 73). Companion write-up, additional larger certificates through r = 167 (not packaged in this single repository due to certificate size), and dated literature search logs are published at https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/odd-perfect-equal-exponents. Coverage by this package's Palomar comparison: of the companion paper's 3 main results, 1 is compared in Lean in full (33%; Theorem 1) and 1 in part (Theorem 2 for the 20 odd primes r <= 73; its cases r = 79 and 83, which the paper reports as checked in its own Lean library, are not in this package); Theorem 3 (89 <= r <= 167) is by certificate only. Abstract claims: the same 3 results, with the same split.
entries.title: Odd Perfect Numbers: Equal Non-Special Exponents for Every Odd Prime 3 <= r <= 73

entries.abstract: For n >= 1 let a(n) = Sum_{k=0}^{n-1} C(n, k) C(n-1, k) C(n+k-1, k)^2 and a(0) = 1 (OEIS A212334). This package gives original machine-checked proofs of both of Peter Bala's open supercongruence conjectures on a(n): a(p) ≡ 1 (mod p^5) for every prime p >= 5 (conjecture_1, Dec 12, 2021), and a(p^r) ≡ a(p^{r-1}) (mod p^{3r+3}) for every prime p >= 5 and integer r >= 2 (conjecture_2, Oct 13, 2022).
entries.title: OEIS A212334: Peter Bala's mod p^5 and mod p^(3r+3) supercongruence conjectures

entries.abstract: The exact two-colour book Ramsey number R(B5,B9) is 29. The proof combines a 28-vertex explicit colouring, degree and deficit identities, a finite degree classification, and elimination of all surviving 29-vertex cases. The formal statement asserts the least order forcing a red five-page or blue nine-page book. Originality is not independently confirmed.
entries.title: Exact determination of the book Ramsey number R(B5,B9) = 29

entries.abstract: Standalone, zero-dependency Lean 4 formalization of a new unconditional upper bound for Erdős Problem #128 (the Sparse Halves Conjecture for triangle-free graphs): every finite simple triangle-free graph G on n vertices contains an induced subgraph on floor(n / 2) vertices spanning at most (261 / 10000) * n^2 = 0.0261 * n^2 undirected edges, strictly improving Alexander Razborov's unconditional upper bound of (27 / 1024) * n^2 ≈ 0.0263671875 * n^2 (Sbornik: Mathematics, 2022). The proof combines a pure-integer concavity rounding theorem, a family of symmetric fractional-half pointwise inequalities (including non-edge union inequalities), an inductive canonical classification of all 107 non-isomorphic triangle-free 7-vertex graphs, and an exact integer Flag Algebra sum-of-squares certificate of order N = 7 using 18 rank-1 squares, verified entirely inside the Lean 4 kernel without floating point, native_decide, or external library dependencies.
entries.title: Erdős Problem #128: Improved Unconditional Sparse Halves Bound (261/10000)

entries.abstract:
The graph polynomial (Kirchhoff polynomial, first Symanzik polynomial) of a finite multigraph is Psi = sum over spanning trees T of the product of the edge variables alpha_e for e not in T. Its zero set, the graph hypersurface, carries the Feynman periods of the graph, and Kontsevich asked whether its number of points over a finite field with q elements is always a polynomial in q. This is false in general (Belkale–Brosnan 2003; explicit counterexamples have 14 edges) but true for small graphs. This entry proves in Lean 4 and Mathlib that it holds for every series–parallel graph, together with the combinatorial rules behind it and exact counts for two families. Seven statements are compared.
(1)-(4) Series and parallel rules. For two-terminal multigraphs, let Phi be the 2-forest polynomial (sum over spanning 2-forests separating the terminals of the product of the variables of the edges outside the forest). Under series composition Psi = Psi1 Psi2 and Phi = Phi1 Psi2 + Psi1 Phi2; under parallel composition Psi = Psi1 Phi2 + Phi1 Psi2 and Phi = Phi1 Phi2, with the two edge sets disjoint. (In the electrical reading, with alpha_e the resistance of edge e, Phi/Psi is the effective resistance between the terminals.) (5) For every series–parallel graph (built from single edges by series and parallel composition) there is a single integer polynomial P such that, for every finite field with q elements, the affine graph hypersurface {a : Psi(a) = 0} has exactly P(q) points. (6) For the banana graph with m parallel edges (Psi = e_(m-1)) the count is q^m - (q-1)^m - m(q-1)^(m-1) + ((q-1)^m + (-1)^m (q-1))/q, stated multiplied by q. (7) For K4, the smallest graph that is not series–parallel, the count is q^2 (q^3 + q - 1).
The proof of (5) tracks four counts per graph: the points where Psi and Phi both vanish, only Psi vanishes, only Phi vanishes, and neither vanishes. Psi and Phi are homogeneous of consecutive degrees, so scaling all variables by a nonzero constant scales the ratio Phi/Psi by that constant; hence on the last set the ratio is equidistributed over the nonzero field elements. With this the four counts of a series or parallel composition are explicit polynomial functions of the counts of the parts, and induction gives (5). The count (7) is proved by eliminating one variable at a time, using that Psi is linear in each variable.
The results are known in substance: polynomiality for series–parallel graphs follows from Stembridge's reductions (1998) and is stated by Brown and Schnetz (2012), citing Aluffi and Marcolli; the banana and K4 counts are classical. We did not find the (Psi, Phi) series–parallel rules or the equidistribution argument stated in this form in the literature. We searched Mathlib (source and pull requests), other Lean repositories via GitHub code search, the Isabelle AFP, Coq/Rocq, HOL, Agda, Mizar and the Palomar registry (November 2026) and found no earlier formalization of graph hypersurfaces or of Kontsevich's question; priority is nevertheless unknown.
entries.title: Point counts of graph hypersurfaces: Kontsevich's polynomiality holds for every series–parallel graph, with the series–parallel rules for the graph and 2-forest polynomials and the exact counts for banana graphs and K4

entries.abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of five statements about the factor languages of substitutions. Call a length L oriented when no factor of length L has its reversal among the factors; being oriented passes to every longer length, and fails at L when some factor of length L is a palindrome. The orientation threshold is the least oriented length (one more than the greatest length of a reflected factor). (1) For every n >= 3, the substitution sigma_n on the letters 1, ..., n, i -> i+1 (i < n), n -> 1 2, whose incidence matrix has characteristic polynomial x^n - x - 1, has orientation threshold exactly 4 from the seed 1: some factor of length three is its own reversal (1 2 1), and every factor of length at least four has a reversal that is not a factor. One proof covers every n: the certificate is a set of index rules checked by omega, not an enumeration. n = 3 is the cubic Padovan substitution a -> b, b -> c, c -> ab and n = 4 the quartic substitution a -> b, b -> c, c -> d, d -> ab. (2) For every letter 1 <= x <= n, the factor language of sigma_n from x is the one from 1. (3) The same as (1) for the twelve-letter tensor product of the cubic and the quartic substitution on {p, q, r} x {1, 2, 3, 4}, seed p1 (q1 q2 q1); its incidence matrix is the Kronecker product, with characteristic polynomial the minimal polynomial of rho Q (the product of the two real roots greater than one). The tensor is not a member of the family. (4) The tensor factor language is the same from every seed letter. (5) Statement 3 from every seed and across seeds. No native_decide is used: the family proof is omega and simp, the tensor proof a finite certificate checked by decide / decide +kernel. No physical identification is an axiom, a hypothesis or a conclusion of any statement.
entries.title: The orientation threshold 4 for the substitutions of x^n - x - 1, n >= 3, and the twelve-letter rho Q tensor

entries.abstract: Sharp lower bounds and equality cases for mixed-triangle absorbers of doubled ears, with exact finite optima for two labelled paths and a subdivided claw.
entries.title: Sharp bounds for typed triangle absorbers of doubled ears

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Akmal Xodarev, "On the Structural Foundations of Signature Volatility Models", arXiv:2605.17142. Palomar registration: TBD. Framing: prove the paper claims that hold, at the exact strength of the Lean theorems below, and refute the claims that do not, by Lean negations of those claims and nothing stronger. Theorems A–D and their refutations are stated in unwrapped form, using only definitions built directly from the Brownian driver B: the signature Ŵ_t = paperSig2 B 0 t of (t, W_t), the signature filtration sigFiltration B generated by its coordinates, the volatility sigVol M B = ⟨ℓ, Ŵ_t⟩, the Itô integral kitItoInt B and the quadratic variation kitQuadVar B. Each X_unwrapped is proved from the library theorem X (theorem_A, …), which states the corresponding claim through the ProlongedBrownianSetup / ItoCalculusKit packaging; the unwrapped definitions agree with the packaged ones definitionally. The packaged SignaturePriceSolution represents the price by the Doléans exponential at every outcome; the unwrapped predicate IsSignaturePrice requires almost surely continuous paths on [0, T] and almost sure equality to that exponential at each time. Compared: theorem_A_unwrapped, theorem_B_mp_unwrapped, theorem_D_unwrapped (proved); not_affine_riccati_duality_mpr_unwrapped, not_affine_riccati_duality_unwrapped, not_theorem_B_mpr_unwrapped, not_theorem_B_unwrapped, not_theorem_C_unwrapped, theorem_D_residual_hypothesis_fails_unwrapped, not_literal_nflvr_unwrapped, not_terminal_bdd_nflvr_unwrapped (refutations). Proved: theorem_A_unwrapped — for every SignatureVolatilityModel (which includes d ≥ 1, T > 0, s₀ > 0, HypH1, HypH2, and parameter nondegeneracy ℓ ≠ 0) and every Brownian driver, under the additional analytic hypothesis HypH3 on the signature volatility, there exists a price process S with IsSignaturePrice (S₀ = s₀, measurable, adapted to the signature filtration, strictly positive, with almost surely continuous paths on [0, T] and, at each t ∈ [0, T], almost sure equality to the Doléans exponential s₀ exp(∫σ dW − ½∫σ² ds), satisfying the integral equation S_t = s₀ + ∫_0^t S σ dW almost surely for each t ∈ [0, T], with square-integrable supremum, and a martingale on the signature filtration), and S is unique among processes that are measurable with respect to the signature filtration, lie in KitStrongSolutionClass, and satisfy the integral equation, almost everywhere on [0, T]; theorem_B_mp_unwrapped — under the same HypH3, there exists such an S that is a martingale on the signature filtration, SatisfiesNFLVR_DS holds for the Delbaen–Schachermayer cone BoundedBelowGains of uniformly bounded-below admissible strategies whose integrand H S σ lies in the ℱ^W-predictable L² space and whose wealth is a continuous genuine L² Itô integral against W⁰ (narrower than the paper's local class ∫ H² d⟨S⟩ < ∞ almost surely), for that same process S, every signature coordinate is a special semimartingale for the signature filtration, and the Riccati conjunct is the immediate implication that a classical Riccati solution satisfying the exponential dual formula yields a classical Riccati solution (recorded as stated, not a substantive forward pricing result). This is not a proof of the paper's full Theorem B, whose conjunction includes the ← pricing direction of the iff; theorem_D_unwrapped — for every Market (a model, a Brownian driver and HypH3, with price S = sigPrice, the Doléans exponential) and every X in L²(ℱ^S_T), there is a unique GKW decomposition X = (∫ X) · 1 + G + ε with G in the gains space H0 and orthogonal to constants, ε in L²(ℱ^S_T) ∩ H0⊥ and orthogonal to the gains set, and the Pythagorean identity. This does not identify G as a stochastic integral ∫ H dS. Refuted by Lean counterexamples: not_affine_riccati_duality_mpr_unwrapped — for every SignatureVolatilityModel and every Brownian driver, with no analytic HypH3 hypothesis, it is not the case that every finitely supported u₀ with finite signature transform and some classical Riccati solution admits a classical Riccati solution ψ for which E[exp⟨u₀, Ŵ_T⟩ | ℱ_t] = exp⟨ψ(T − t), Ŵ_t⟩ almost surely for all t ∈ [0, T]. The proof uses the family u₀^(λ) = 2λ e_[1,1,1] − λ e_[1,0] − 12λ² e_[1,1,1,1,0] (λ ≥ 1), for which ℛ(u₀^(λ)) = 0 and the signature transform is finite (Lean proves ∫ exp⟨u₀^(λ), Ŵ_t⟩ dP ≤ 1). Lean does not state a theorem that this exponential is a local martingale or that it is not a true martingale; what is compared is the failure of the universal conditional-expectation formula; not_affine_riccati_duality_unwrapped — under the same hypotheses (every model and driver, no HypH3), the paper's iff in Theorem 4.2(ii) is false as a universal statement over such u₀; not_theorem_B_mpr_unwrapped and not_theorem_B_unwrapped — the same ← failure, and the failure of the paper's full Theorem B conjunction, each stated with an additional unused HypH3 hypothesis, so they apply to every model and driver for which analytic HypH3 holds (HypH3 is satisfiable; it holds for constant volatility); not_theorem_C_unwrapped — for the Black–Scholes market (T > 0, s₀ > 0, σ₀ ≠ 0, one-dimensional Brownian motion) and every finite set of call strikes, the unconditional equivalence "complete with finitely many calls on ℱ^S_T ⇔ N^*_S < ∞" is false, and the paper's separate claim that Black–Scholes has completeness depth N^*_S = 0 is likewise false: the market is complete, but under Definition 55 one has N^*_S = ∞. This is not a counterexample inside Theorem 56's finite-polynomial subcase K(N^*_S) < ∞ with a strike set rich enough to span polynomials in S_T of degree at most K(N^*_S). Here complete means that every X in L²(ℱ^S_T) is almost surely c + Σ_k a_k (S_T − k)^+ + G with G in the L²-closed span of the elementary Brownian integrals Σ_p h_p (W_{p.2} − W_{p.1}) over intervals 0 ≤ p.1 ≤ p.2 ≤ T with h_p bounded and σ(W_u : u ≤ p.1)-measurable; theorem_D_residual_hypothesis_fails_unwrapped — for Black–Scholes (same parameters as above), ¬ (N^*_S < ∞). This shows that the residual-expansion hypothesis of Theorem D fails for Black–Scholes; it does not refute the expansion identity on markets where the hypothesis holds; not_literal_nflvr_unwrapped — for Black–Scholes (T > 0, s₀ > 0, σ₀ ≠ 0, 1-dimensional Brownian motion), literal NFLVR (Defs 2.17 and 4.3, no wealth lower bound) fails: a geometric-grid doubling strategy, transferred by H = K/(S σ₀), is S-admissible and ends at V_T = 1 a.s.; not_terminal_bdd_nflvr_unwrapped — the same free lunch is in the terminal- only bounded-below cone of Section 4.6. Neither claim refutes Delbaen–Schachermayer NFLVR, which requires a uniform-in-time lower bound and, in the Lean statement, an integrand H S σ in ℱ^W-predictable L² with wealth a continuous genuine L² Itô integral against W⁰, narrower than the paper's local class, and is proved at that strength for the unwrapped signature-price process in theorem_B_mp_unwrapped. The geometric-grid doubling construction and the distinction among the three NFLVR wordings, as well as the scaled-tensor disproof of the converse Riccati duality, are due to Gemini Carbon. Supporting results, proved in the library with no sorry but not compared: the wrapped forms theorem_A, theorem_B_mp, theorem_D, not_affine_riccati_duality_mpr, not_affine_riccati_duality, not_theorem_B_mpr, not_theorem_B, not_theorem_C (with MathFin's Itô integral of square-integrable predictable integrands as the gains), theorem_D_residual_hypothesis_fails, not_literal_nflvr and not_terminal_bdd_nflvr; affine_riccati_duality_mp — for every model and driver and every finitely supported u₀ with finite signature transform, the immediate implication that a classical Riccati solution satisfying the exponential dual formula yields a classical Riccati solution (recorded as stated, not a substantive forward pricing result); theorem_C_refuted — the same refutation of the unconditional equivalence and of the Black–Scholes depth claim as not_theorem_C; blackScholes_isCompleteWithCalls — Black–Scholes is complete on ℱ^S_T with finitely many calls, for every finite strike set; theorem_C_blackScholes_depth_infinite and blackScholes_completenessDepth_eq_top — its completeness depth is infinite; theorem_C_depth_infinite — N^*_S = ∞ and no finite-depth signature span is dense, for every MarketData whose L²(ℱ^S_T) is infinite-dimensional; not_prop58_blackScholes_depth_zero — Black–Scholes completeness depth is not 0; not_lemma77_shuffle_estimate — for every weight w and every letter ℓ in Fin d, there is no constant C such that ‖e_I ⧢ e_J‖_w ≤ C ‖e_I‖_w ‖e_J‖_w for all words I, J; not_lemma77_of_hypH2 is the same conclusion with an unused HypH2 hypothesis, hence also for every H2 weight; not_lemma78_local_lipschitz — only for the weight w ≡ 1 (Weight.constOne), on ExtTensorAlgebra (d+2) for every d, the Riccati operator is not locally Lipschitz on bounded subsets of T_w. Every compared claim is either proved or refuted at the stated strength. A short mathematical narrative is given for each counterexample. Every compared theorem uses only propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice. Project rule: no Lean `axiom` declarations. Akmal Xodarev did not participate in or endorse this formalization. Lean was written with AI-agent assistance under Lars Warren Ericson's direction and review.
entries.title: Xodarev Signature Volatility Models in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Zero-dependency Lean 4 formalization of two results of Erdős and Gyárfás (1999) associated with Erdős Problem #617: (1) for every prime p — and consequently for arbitrarily large primes p >= N by Euclid's theorem — the complete graph K_{p^2} admits a symmetric balanced p-coloring where every (p + 1)-subset contains edges of all p colors, constructed via finite affine planes AG(2, p); and (2) every symmetric 3-coloring of K_10 contains a 4-vertex subset missing at least one color, proved via a single-color diamond-free extremal degree and triangle-counting argument.
entries.title: Erdős Problem #617: Balanced Colorings for Prime r^2 and r = 3

entries.abstract: For r ≥ 4 and 1 ≤ j ≤ r − 3, a finite r-uniform hypergraph with at least one edge has zero uniform Turán density at level j exactly when its vertices admit an ordering in which each shared (j + 1)-set occupies the same positions in the edges containing it. For any family of such forbidden graphs, a positive uniform Turán density is at least N⁻ᴺ, where N is the binomial coefficient r choose (j + 1). This covers infinite forbidden families as well as finite ones. The development formalizes Theorem 1.1 of Heng Li and Xizhi Liu.
entries.title: Hypergraphs with zero uniform Turán density at intermediate levels

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that symmetric informationally complete POVMs (SIC-POVMs) exist in every finite dimension. The compared statement is OpenQuantumProblem23.sicPOVMs from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, the existence form of Open Quantum Problem 23 and of Zauner's conjecture: for every d >= 1 there are d^2 unit vectors in C^d whose pairwise squared overlaps all equal 1/(d+1). The configuration also compares the eleven benchmark theorems of the same file, which state the cases d = 56, 58, 59, 60, 64, 68, 69, 70, 71, 72 and 75. The mathematics is due to Radchenko and Wheeler, who build the required vectors from special values of the modular quantum dilogarithm and show by class field theory that a suitable Galois automorphism exists, together with the reduction of Appleby, Flammia and Kopp from such "ghost" vectors to SIC-POVMs. The Lean proof follows the argument of these sources in five parts: the reduction to a ghost fiducial with a unimodular Galois flip, the finite identities for the special values, their algebraicity by a 2-adic argument, the analytic properties of Faddeev's quantum dilogarithm, and the reciprocity argument through ray class fields, Artin reciprocity and the Chebotarev density theorem. Class field theory comes from the external Lean library of N. Yamaguchi and the Chebotarev density theorem from a vendored, ported copy of the library of C. Birkbeck. The repository also proves, as a further result outside the compared configuration, the existence of rank-r SICs of Appleby, Flammia and Kopp for r >= 1, d > 2r + 1 and r(d - r) dividing d^2 - 1. All proofs depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and no sorry remains outside the deliberate placeholders of the Challenge. An earlier, independent Lean formalization of SIC existence by Māris Ozols exists, with its own statements.
entries.title: SIC-POVMs exist in every dimension (Open Quantum Problem 23): a Lean 4 formalization

entries.abstract: Fifteen explicit homogeneous rays determine a full-dimensional convex four-polytope. Its face lattice admits a realization over a subfield of the reals if and only if that subfield contains the square root of five. In particular this face lattice has no rational realization.
entries.title: A nonrational four-polytope with fifteen vertices

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof of Gross's discrete Hudson theorem: for odd d, a pure state of n qudits has a non-negative Wigner function if and only if it is a stabilizer state. Every odd d is covered, including composite d, and every n. The definitions follow Gross's Section II: the Weyl operators w(p, q) with the symmetric phase convention, the phase point operators A(a) = d^(-n) sum_b omega([a, b]) w(b), the Wigner function W(a) = d^(-n) <psi|A(a)|psi>, and a stabilizer state as a common eigenvector of the Weyl operators of an isotropic subgroup of phase space with d^n elements. Also proved: the Wigner function is real, and equals the closed form d^(-n) sum_xi omega(p . xi) conj(psi(q + xi/2)) psi(q - xi/2) (Gross, Theorem 6.2, after xi -> -xi), and the equivalence of the definition with Gross's Lemma 8 form, where the eigenvalues are omega([v, m])^(-1). The proof does not follow Gross's Section III; it follows the route of Gross, Nezami and Walter (2021), Section 8.1. For a pure state the Wigner values sum to 1, their squares sum to d^(-n), and none exceeds d^(-n), so non-negative values are 0 or d^(-n); at the d^n points where W = d^(-n) the phase point operators fix the state, and products of two of them give a maximal isotropic group of Weyl operators of which the state is a common eigenvector. The converse is a character sum. Controls show both sides of the equivalence are attained, including at the composite dimension d = 9.
entries.title: The discrete Hudson theorem

entries.abstract: Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of 7 statements on tilings of a rectangle by congruent copies of one polyomino (rotations and reflections allowed): a crossing statement, two statements on tiles that hold two corner cells, the three-copy theorem (printed prior work, proved here a second time), a statement that reduces 3 and 5 copies at a given number of cells to a finite search, the statement that case (I) of five copies does not occur (Theorem A18), and Corollary A19. Corollary A19 is proved in Lean: no rectangle is tiled by exactly five congruent copies of a polyomino that is not a rectangle. Proved in Lean with standard axioms only: 7 of 7 statements, all witnessed. AI research agents built and directed by Tyler B. Hughes generated and checked this work. No human mathematician has yet refereed the proof.
entries.title: Five congruent copies of a non-rectangular polyomino do not tile a rectangle, with the three-copy theorem

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Conjecture 61 of DeLaViña's "Written on the Wall II" (conjectures of Graffiti.pc): for every finite simple connected graph G on at least two vertices, the number f(G) of vertices of a largest induced forest satisfies f(G) ≥ residue(G) + ⌈diam(G)/3⌉, where residue(G) is the Havel–Hakimi residue of the degree sequence. The formal statement is the one recorded in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (WrittenOnTheWallII/GraphConjecture61.lean, theorem `conjecture61`, tagged research open there on 26 November 2026), copied verbatim together with its definitions of the residue and of `largestInducedForestSize`. The proof marks ⌈diam/3⌉ disjoint edges on a diametral geodesic and proves a new lemma: if a vertex set U induces a perfect matching, there is an independent set S outside U with residue(G) ≤ |S| + ⌈|U \ N(S)|/2⌉. The lemma is obtained by a maximum-degree deletion argument with the matching re-paired in deletion order; the classical fact that deleting a maximum-degree vertex does not decrease the residue is proved from the Havel–Hakimi recursion.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 61: f(G) ≥ residue(G) + ⌈diam(G)/3⌉

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization proving Written on the Wall II Conjecture 61: for every nontrivial finite connected simple graph G, the maximum order f(G) of an induced forest satisfies f(G) ≥ residue(G) + ⌈diam(G) / 3⌉, where residue(G) is the Havel-Hakimi residue and diam(G) is the graph diameter. The proof establishes positive maximum-degree vertex-deletion monotonicity for Havel-Hakimi residue from first principles via degree-sequence exchanges and Havel-Hakimi graphicality, proves a matching-residue theorem yielding the general Induced-Matching Residue Inequality R(G) ≤ max(α(G - A), α(G - B)) for every induced matching A ↔ B in any finite simple graph G, applies it to ⌈diam(G) / 3⌉ edges along a diametral geodesic whose sides are 3-packings, and lifts the bound to the exact real-valued statement in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures using only the three standard Lean axioms.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 61: Induced Forest, Residue, and Diameter Bound in Lean 4

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof establishing the sharp additive inequality τ(T) ≤ γ_t(T) + p(T) - 2 for every finite simple tree T on at least two vertices with path cover number p(T) ≥ 2, where τ(T) is the vertex cover number, γ_t(T) is the total domination number, and p(T) is the minimum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint paths covering V(T) (singletons allowed). Because γ_t(T) + p(T) - 2 ≤ γ_t(T) · (p(T) - 1) for all γ_t ≥ 2 and p ≥ 2 (strictly stronger whenever p ≥ 3), this immediately proves all three upstream statements of Written on the Wall II Conjecture 372 in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (conjecture372, variants.two_paths, and variants.regularized). The formal proof uses an original rooted-tree structural induction certified by a kernel-checked finite-state potential table, bridged directly to Mathlib's SimpleGraph.IsTree and SimpleGraph.vertexCoverNum with only the standard axioms.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 372: Sharp Additive Tree Bound in Lean 4

entries.abstract: This project formalizes Theorems 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3 of the supplied V4 manuscript on Turing universality in hypergraph Turán theory. Theorem 1.1 gives a primitive-recursive compiler from binary words to single finite simple three-uniform hypergraphs: ordinary Turán density equals a fixed rational threshold exactly on nonhalting inputs and exceeds it exactly on halting inputs. Theorem 1.2 extends the density dichotomy to finite forbidden families in every uniformity at least three, with joint primitive-recursive compilers, exact density scaling, and input-independent globally optimal templates whose blowups avoid the compiled families. Theorem 1.3 provides a jointly primitive-recursive structural compiler above a fixed rank threshold. Nonhalting inputs have one ordinary extremal profile and edge-edit stability with fixed finite role patterns and exact balanced class sizes. Halting inputs have two disjoint nonempty compact phases, separated by fixed finite test graphs, each homeomorphic to the entire inner extremal space. The package includes the finite computation, obstruction, extremal, suspension, and effective-construction proofs needed for these three results. One independent Challenge and one Comparator configuration select all three theorem declarations.
entries.title: Turing Universality in Hypergraph Turán Theory

entries.abstract: For a finite set A of positive integers let f_A(t) = sum over a in A of cos(2 pi a t), and call D(A) = -min_t f_A(t) the depth of A. Chowla conjectured in 1965 that there is an absolute constant c > 0 such that every nonempty A satisfies min_t f_A(t) < -c sqrt(|A|) (Chowla's cosine problem; Erdős Problem #510). This project is a complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of a counterexample from the manuscript "A prime-square counterexample to Chowla's cosine conjecture" (included as manuscript/chowla_prime_square.pdf): for every eps > 0 there are arbitrarily large finite sets A of positive integers with f_A(t) > -eps sqrt(|A|) for every real t. The manuscript, including the counterexample and its proof, was produced by the AI model Astra 6.2, prompted by Shengtong Zhang. The Lean formalization was then written by Claude Opus 5.5 agents in Cursor. Two theorems are compared. The main one, `Erdos510.erdos_510`, is the negation of the statement of Erdős Problem #510 in Google DeepMind's formal-conjectures repository, copied verbatim from FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/510.lean at commit 7db2ea3 (where it is tagged research open). The second, `cosine_counterexample`, is Theorem 1 of the manuscript, which states exactly the result above. The proof follows the manuscript. A binary profile given by horizontal slices of an annulus is smoothed so that a Fourier multiplier in the logarithm of the radius (computed through the Laplace and Mellin transforms of the Bessel function J_0 and Legendre duplication) produces a family with nonnegative Fourier transform. Auxiliary circle coordinates make the label frequencies primitive integer vectors, a Chinese remainder construction maps them to multiplicatively independent integers, and characters modulo a prime square with an explicit Gauss-sum identity and equidistributed phases realize the required multipliers. Poisson summation over residue classes gives a lower bound for the weighted cosine sum, and the weights are rounded to a set using Spencer's discrepancy theorem, which is proved here from a partial-colouring lemma, together with a discrete de la Vallée-Poussin interpolation bound. The proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: A counterexample to Chowla's cosine conjecture
